mission.name: Crumb And Kettle
mission.description: The Crumb & Kettle bakery prints its oven schedule from Terraform. Someone edited main.tf at 4 a.m. and now every command dies with a parser error before the first loaf is planned.
mission.objective: Make the configuration parse and apply so bakery/oven-schedule.txt lists the three batches (05:30 sourdough, 06:15 rye, 07:00 focaccia), one per line, and bakery/dough-card.txt still exists.

mission.name: Quayside Lane Bookings
mission.description: The Quayside public swimming baths keeps its lane booking sheet in Terraform. After a late-night edit, terraform refuses to read the file and complains about block types it has never heard of.
mission.objective: Fix the misspelled top-level block keywords so the configuration applies and lanes/booking.txt reads "Lane: Lane 4 (fast, 25 m)" and "Slot length: 3h" on two lines. Keep the lane variable and the booking_path output.

mission.name: Thistledown Apiary
mission.description: A beekeeper's inspection log is generated by Terraform, but terraform init fails before any hive is counted. The error talks about a provider that cannot be found in the registry.
mission.objective: Make terraform init succeed by correcting the provider's source address, then apply so apiary/inspection.txt lists both hives and the total_bees output is 84500.

mission.name: Fete Tombola Draw
mission.description: The village fête draws its tombola winner with Terraform, but init stops with complaints about "invalid version constraint" for two providers, so no ticket can be drawn.
mission.objective: Repair both provider version constraints so terraform init works (keep a constraint on each of the two providers) and the winning ticket, a number from 100 to 499, is written to fete/stage-board.txt.

mission.name: Saltmarsh Tide Card
mission.description: The harbour office tide card used to build fine, but today every Terraform command stops immediately with a message about the Terraform version being unsupported by the configuration.
mission.objective: Update the version gate in terraform.tf so the installed Terraform is accepted (the gate must stay in place) and harbour/tides.csv is written with its header and two port rows.

mission.name: Marlowe Museum Placards
mission.description: The spring exhibition placards are generated by Terraform. One of the strings is missing a quote, and the error messages complain about newlines and strings in places that look perfectly fine.
mission.objective: Fix the string so the config applies. placards/gallery-4.txt must hold two lines (the gallery title and "Curated by Ines Calloway") and placards/gallery-7.txt must be untouched.

mission.name: Copper Kettle Menu
mission.description: The tavern's menu board file is generated from a heredoc, and the front-of-house tablet shows every line pushed four spaces to the right. The cook wants the file to match the config's text shape.
mission.objective: Make tavern/menu.txt start at column 0 (the title and closing line unindented) while keeping the two-space indent of the three dish lines under the title. Keep the soup variable in use.

mission.name: Kestrel Ridge Bulletin
mission.description: The mountain weather station publishes a daily bulletin from Terraform variables. The plan is happy, but the published bulletin shows raw text such as "$(var.station)" where the numbers should be.
mission.objective: Make weather/bulletin.txt contain the real values of the station, altitude_m and wind_knots variables on three lines ("Station: Kestrel Ridge", "Altitude: 1840 m", "Wind: 23 knots") and keep them driven by the variables.

mission.name: Dome Three Watering
mission.description: Terraform generates the watering shell script for the Dome 3 greenhouse. The script is supposed to use shell variables such as HOME and PUMP_SECONDS, but Terraform stops with errors about references it does not know.
mission.objective: Make dome3/water.sh contain the bay name filled in by Terraform and the shell expressions ${HOME} and ${PUMP_SECONDS:-30} written literally, so the script is valid bash.

mission.name: Buzzer Row Quiz Show
mission.description: The Buzzer Row TV game show picks its first-round questions with Terraform. The plan stops with complaints that a number is required, and the show host swears he typed the numbers in plain English.
mission.objective: Make the config apply with 8 contestants (contestant_count output = 8) and exactly 3 distinct questions picked in round one. Both values must be real numbers in the config.

mission.name: Driftwood Wi-Fi Vouchers
mission.description: The hostel's guest Wi-Fi vouchers come from random_string, tuned for a label printer that can only print capital letters and digits. Terraform now refuses the character-class settings, even though "yes" and "enabled" were perfectly clear to the author.
mission.objective: Make the voucher an 8-character code made only of capital letters and digits (A-Z, 0-9). Use real true/false values for the character-class arguments, and write the code to hostel/voucher-slip.txt.

mission.name: Static And Signal Slugs
mission.description: A podcast team generates episode URL slugs with random_pet and lets editors override the word separator. Without an override the slugs come out glued together as "epwisefox" instead of the usual "ep-wise-fox".
mission.objective: With slug_separator unset the slug must look like ep-word-word (the provider default separator); with -var slug_separator=_ it must use underscores. Don't hard-code the separator.

mission.name: Wax And Groove Prices
mission.description: A record shop prices its used sleeves with Terraform. The owner's notes were pasted in as comments, using the styles of SQL, an INI file and HTML, and now Terraform cannot even read the file.
mission.objective: Make the file parse using comment syntax HCL understands, and write shop/price-list.csv with one "title,price" line per record, prices rounded to two decimals after the 10 percent markup.

mission.name: Alder Hollow Seed Vault
mission.description: The community seed library prints one label per seed lot and wants later inspector changes to leave the label alone. The author wrote two settings as if they were attributes, and Terraform says they are not expected there.
mission.objective: Fix the configuration so it applies and writes vault/label-BEAN-2031.txt, and so that changing the inspector variable later produces no plan changes (content changes are ignored). Use proper nested blocks.

mission.name: Marta And Idris Invitations
mission.description: A wedding invitation is stitched together from two text snippets kept in the templates/ folder. Terraform stops during plan, claiming that it cannot find either file.
mission.objective: Make letters/invitation.txt contain the greeting, the header snippet and the footer snippet from templates/. Reference the snippets with paths anchored to the module directory, not the shell's current directory.

mission.name: Ribeira River Run
mission.description: A city marathon's paperwork is split across main.tf, bibs.tf and outputs.tf, and all three read inputs through var.something. Terraform says those inputs were never declared.
mission.objective: Declare the three missing input variables in a new variables.tf with these defaults: race_city = "Porto", runner_count = 1200 and first_bib = 1001 (both numbers). The race sheet and bib range must then follow those variables.

mission.name: Inkwell Row Flash Sheets
mission.description: The studio prints one flash sheet per design. A colleague copied the swallow flash sheet into a new file for the autumn flash event, and now Terraform refuses to load the module because something is declared twice.
mission.objective: Keep both designs. After applying, flash/swallow.txt and flash/anchor.txt must both exist with their own text, and state must hold two local_file resources.

mission.name: Fenwick Cheese Cellar
mission.description: The cheese cellar prints a label for every maturing wheel from a block of named constants. Terraform rejects the constants block and, once that is out of the way, every place that reads them.
mission.objective: Declare the constants with the right block keyword and read them with the right reference prefix, so cellar/wheel-label.txt shows the cheese, rind, weight and a price of 248 EUR (8 kg times 31 per kg). The price must be computed from the other two values.

mission.name: Brightwell Filament Shelf
mission.description: The makerspace prints labels for its filament spools from Terraform. The names a volunteer chose for a variable and two resources look natural to a human, but Terraform will not accept them as identifiers.
mission.objective: Rename the offending identifiers consistently so the config applies. shelf/label.txt and shelf/tag.txt must mention "signal orange", and the outputs label_path and tag_path must point at those files.

mission.name: Kestrel Street Timetable
mission.description: The tram depot's CI pipeline now runs "terraform fmt -check -recursive" before anything else, and the timetable repository fails it on every file, including one tucked away in a subfolder.
mission.objective: Reformat the repository so terraform fmt -check -recursive passes with no output. Keep the files (including extras/depot-notes.tf) and the same behaviour: depot/line-7.txt and depot/stop-count.txt unchanged.

mission.name: Toy Factory Shift Board
mission.description: The Tinkertop toy factory prints everything in its out/ folder and pins it beside the assembly line. Since the last change the daily shift board keeps landing in the project root, where nobody looks, while the pallet labels are filed correctly.
mission.objective: Write the shift board to out/shift-board.txt (inside the module directory, like the pallet labels) and make nothing be left behind as shift-board.txt in the project root.

mission.name: Lift Closed Badge
mission.description: Pinecrest Ridge's lift-status signage needs a real PNG file for its red CLOSED badge. The config was written in a hurry, passing the picture to local_file twice, and Terraform refuses to even plan it.
mission.objective: Make signage/lift-closed.png a valid PNG image whose bytes are the base64-decoded badge from the config. Keep both local_file resources and keep the picture in base64 form.

mission.name: Vending Fleet Tokens
mission.description: The Hollowmere vending fleet's sync agent will not start unless its token file is private to the owner, and the depot scanner needs the manifest readable by everybody. The permission arguments in the config are written the way chmod would never accept them.
mission.objective: Create fleet/sync.token with mode 0600 and fleet/machines.csv with mode 0644, and give the fleet/ directory mode 0755. Keep both resources and keep using the file_permission arguments.

mission.name: Library Card Numbers
mission.description: The Marlowe Street library's card scanner only accepts 10 characters of lowercase letters and digits. The generated card numbers come out too long and full of capitals and punctuation, and the scanner keeps beeping at them.
mission.objective: Make random_string.card_number produce exactly 10 characters matching ^[a-z0-9]{10}$ and keep the card file in cards/new-member.txt showing that number.

mission.name: Lucky Strike Jackpot Draw
mission.description: The Lucky Strike bingo hall's jackpot draw is drawn by Terraform to keep the caller honest, but the draw refuses to run at all. Management insists the cards still run from 1000 to 1499.
mission.objective: Draw a winning card between 1000 and 1499 inclusive using random_integer.winning_card, keep the locals as they are, and have hall/winner.txt announce that card.

mission.name: Cobalt Yard Audio Guide Pass
mission.description: The Cobalt Yard Castle Ruins Visitor Centre generates a fresh audio-guide app password for each day pass, but the voucher printer has been silent since someone tightened the password rules. Terraform will not produce a password at all.
mission.objective: Keep the password at 12 characters and make it contain at least 2 uppercase, 2 lowercase, 2 digits and 2 special characters. The day-pass voucher file must contain the generated password.

mission.name: Parcel Locker Codes
mission.description: Quillfeather Post issues each parcel-locker drop a UUID as its pickup code. The ticket writer and the pickup_code output both stopped working after a refactor, and the error talks about an attribute that apparently does not exist.
mission.objective: Make lockers/ticket.json contain the drop_id and receipt UUIDs generated by the two random_uuid resources, and have the pickup_code output return the drop_id UUID.

mission.name: Donkey Nicknames
mission.description: Cragmoor Donkey Sanctuary names its donkeys with random pet names so sponsors can book visits with them on a shared calendar. The jack's nickname is accepted by the sponsor card, but the jenny's nickname is rejected every time.
mission.objective: Make both nicknames match ^donkey-[a-z]+-[a-z]+$ (the prefix, then exactly two words, separated by hyphens). Keep both resources and have the sponsor card list them.

mission.name: Darkroom Batch Tags
mission.description: Silverhalide Darkroom stamps a 12 character hex tag on each film canister, but the tags coming out of Terraform are long, mixed-case, and contain dashes and underscores. The logbook scanner rejects them and the log file names are a mess too.
mission.objective: Make the batch tag exactly 12 lowercase hex characters (^[0-9a-f]{12}$), use it in the batch_tag output and in the logbook file name (logbook/batch-<tag>.txt), and keep the content showing the same tag.

mission.name: Regatta Cue Sheet
mission.description: The Brightwater Regatta fireworks crew re-reads the cue sheet whenever a revision marker changes. The marker resource follows the running order, but Terraform now rejects its triggers with a type error.
mission.objective: Make null_resource.cue_sheet apply with triggers whose values are all strings, keep the running order as the list in locals, and make the cues trigger actually contain every cue name so that changing the order would change the trigger.

mission.name: Print Shop Release Stamp
mission.description: The Inkwell Press print server decides which template bundle is live by reading dist/RELEASE, which a local-exec step is supposed to write after each release. Since the script was tidied, terraform apply fails and no stamp is ever written.
mission.objective: Make the null_resource's local-exec provisioner run successfully and write dist/RELEASE containing exactly the line release=2024.3-rc1 (taken from var.release). Keep it a local- exec provisioner.

mission.name: Drone Fleet Keys
mission.description: Skylark's delivery drones verify telemetry with a P-256 ECDSA key, and the ground stations accept firmware only when it is signed with RSA-4096. Terraform rejects the telemetry key, so neither public key gets published to the fleet-keys folder.
mission.objective: Create the telemetry key as ECDSA on the P256 curve and keep the firmware key as RSA 4096. Both public keys must be written in OpenSSH format to fleet-keys/telemetry.pub and fleet- keys/firmware.pub.

mission.name: Arena Scoreboard Certificate
mission.description: Nightfall Arena runs a LAN-party scoreboard over HTTPS with its own self-signed certificate. The certificate resource will not plan: it is missing something the browsers insist on, and the subject was written in the wrong shape.
mission.objective: Produce pki/scoreboard.pem: a self-signed certificate for scoreboard.arena.lan, organisation Nightfall Arena, usable for server_auth (plus digital_signature and key_encipherment), valid for 72 hours.

mission.name: Offshore Wind Sensor CSR
mission.description: Saltmarsh Offshore Wind generates a key and a signing request for each turbine sensor, and the CA team signs the request. The CSR resource refuses to build, and the error complains about the PEM it was given.
mission.objective: Build pki/turbine-07.csr as a valid certificate request signed by the sensor's own key, so that the public key inside the CSR is the public half of tls_private_key.sensor. Keep the private key file too.

mission.name: Board Game Cafe Slips
mission.description: The Dicewood board-game cafe prints a reservation slip for every group, but the slips all read like source code and the outputs show variable names instead of values. Terraform plans without a single error.
mission.objective: Make hoststand/slip.txt read 'Your table: <table name>, seat <seat number>' using the real generated values, and make the table_name and seat_number outputs return the actual values.

mission.name: Crossword Desk Order
mission.description: At the Marlow Street compiling desk a shell command counts the crossword's clues, so it must run only after clues.txt exists. The author tried to declare that with depends_on, but Terraform complains about both depends_on lists.
mission.objective: Fix both depends_on arguments so they are valid resource references to local_file.clues, keep the clue counter's depends_on, and produce puzzle/clue-count.txt containing 5.

mission.name: Spring Coupon Expiry
mission.description: Marigold Sweets issues a spring coupon that expires fourteen days after it was created. The expiry calculation uses the time provider, but Terraform rejects both the offset value and the attribute the coupon file tries to print.
mission.objective: Make time_offset.expiry exactly 14 days after time_static.issued, and have coupon.txt and the coupon_expires output show the expiry as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

mission.name: Humidor House Records
mission.description: The Cedar Lane cigar humidor house keeps a small record per cigar batch in the built-in terraform_data resource and writes a ageing log from it. Terraform complains that the record's output cannot be configured, and the log references an attribute that is not there.
mission.objective: Store the batch record in terraform_data.batch_record using its input, read it back through its output attribute, and produce humidor/ageing.log reading 'batch=CL-0412 boxes=36' while keeping the triggers_replace on the batch code.

mission.name: Hardware Shop Shelf Rename
mission.description: The Thornfield hardware shop renamed its shelf prefix from yard to depot. The shelf label should follow, but its random_pet is force-new on prefix changes and carries prevent_destroy, so every plan now fails. The shop ledger id next to it must never be replaced.
mission.objective: Get the shelf label replaced with the new depot- prefix and keep the shop ledger UUID exactly as it was, still protected by prevent_destroy. Finish with a clean plan.

mission.name: Garage Build Journal Guard
mission.description: The mechanic at Crumbwell wants Terraform to create the build journal once and then leave it alone, while the work schedule keeps following the config. The ignore_changes list names attributes that local_file does not have, so Terraform refuses the config.
mission.objective: Make Terraform ignore later changes to the build notes' content (the file must keep its original first line) while journal/schedule.txt is updated to the new 12 hour schedule. Do not use ignore_changes = all.

mission.name: Three Machines, No Number
mission.description: The Suds & Sparks laundromat sizes its detergent order from a small Terraform planner. Maya wrote the machine count the way she says it out loud, and now the planner refuses to load at all.
mission.objective: Make terraform apply succeed with machine_count = 3 as a real number, so the output daily_cycles is 120 (3 machines x 40 cycles). Keep the variable's type as number.

mission.name: Maze Off The End
mission.description: The Sunnyfield Sunflower Maze prints its first and last entry slot of the day on a gate board generated by Terraform. After the harvest-season schedule was loaded, the plan began failing on the board's last-entry slot line.
mission.objective: Make terraform apply work so output last_entry is 17:30 for the default timetable, and keep it correct when the entry_times list has a different number of entry slots (the check also plans with 3 and 5 entry slots).

mission.name: Silkworms In The Wrong Tray
mission.description: Mulberry Hill Silk Farm tracks every silkworm's hatch time and tray in a map. The type constraint was copied from the old tray-only file, and terraform refuses to load the new data.
mission.objective: Fix the variable's type constraint so the default loads, 4 tag files are created, slowest_days is 14 and trays_in_use is [A, B, C]. Do not use any; days must stay a number.

mission.name: Menu Without Sizes
mission.description: The Frosty Spoon ice-cream parlour exports its flavour menu to the till through a typed variable. Most flavours come in one size, so the paper menu leaves it blank, and Terraform rejects the tfvars file.
mission.objective: Keep the menu data and make every flavour that omits size end up with size regular, including new entries passed on the command line. Explicit sizes must be kept.

mission.name: The Unordered Window
mission.description: At Reel Deal Video the featured genre in the window is meant to be the alphabetically first genre in the donation boxes. The genres live in a set, and the card generator trips on the first one.
mission.objective: Make featured_genre the alphabetically first genre (animation for the default set) while donated_genres stays a set(string); the check also plans with other genre sets.

mission.name: Reading In The Wrong Order
mission.description: The Ashfall volcano monitoring post publishes a status line for the trailhead warning board from a tuple of station id, temperature and sensor state. Someone typed the default in the order they say it aloud.
mission.objective: Make the configuration valid with the tuple type unchanged, so station_id is summit-vent, temp_c is the number 142.5 and online is the boolean true.

mission.name: The Phantom Hyphen
mission.description: The Aurelia Opera House checks season ticket codes such as ORC-2041 with a validation block. Since it was added, even the default code is rejected, and the box office has started to bypass it.
mission.objective: Fix the validation so ORC-2041 and other well-formed codes (three capital letters, hyphen, four digits) are accepted and everything else is still rejected by the variable's own validation message.

mission.name: Regex Wall Of Text
mission.description: The Spoke & Pedal bike-share app only publishes releases tagged like v3.12. A validation block should explain bad tags politely, but ops only see an unfriendly regex error when the tag is wrong.
mission.objective: Make a malformed release tag fail with the variable's own error message (not a raw regex error), while v3.12 and v10.0 still pass.

mission.name: Null Beats The Default
mission.description: Deepfreeze Backups generates vault policies through a small module with a sensible 30-day default. The pipeline forwards an optional override variable, and since nobody sets it, the module chokes on a null.
mission.objective: Make terraform apply succeed so effective_retention is 30 when no override is given, while -var retention_override=7 still yields 7. The fix belongs in the module's variable declaration; keep passing the root variable straight through.

mission.name: Password In The URL
mission.description: The Granite Gate Mall's concierge-desk tool opens the captive portal admin page through a URL that Terraform builds with the admin password inside. Terraform refuses to plan, complaining about sensitive values.
mission.objective: Make terraform apply succeed while the password stays protected: portal_login_url must be a sensitive output (redacted by terraform output, still the full URL in -json) and the password variable must remain sensitive.

mission.name: Attributes That Don't Exist
mission.description: The Lumen Stock Photo Agency tells its partner portal where the catalogue file lives and what its checksum is through two outputs. Terraform refuses to validate: both outputs reference attributes the file resource does not have.
mission.objective: Fix both outputs so catalogue_path equals the resource's filename and catalogue_checksum equals the SHA-256 of archive/catalogue.csv, read from the resource's exported attributes.

mission.name: Wiki Colon Syndrome
mission.description: The Calder Bay whale-watching sailing notice takes its inputs from terraform.tfvars, which someone pasted from the old ops wiki. Terraform will not even read the file.
mission.objective: Make plain terraform apply read terraform.tfvars and produce the notice for Calder Bay Whale Tours with 14 seats, sailings at 08:30 and 14:15, and compulsory lifejackets. Keep the values in terraform.tfvars (no defaults in the variable blocks).

mission.name: The Unloaded Winter File
mission.description: Birch Room 3's nightly job runs plain terraform apply and still keeps the summer climate settings, even though the winter values sit in prod.tfvars right next to the code. Nothing errors, the saunas are just lukewarm.
mission.objective: Make plain terraform apply (no flags) use the winter settings: target_temp_c 90, vent_mode auto, steam_per_day 6. Keep the defaults in variables.tf as the summer baseline.

mission.name: Dry Run That Won't Leave
mission.description: The Skyward Range prints its launch sequence sheet from the terraform.tfvars that range safety approved: a 45-minute countdown. The printed sheet says five minutes, and nobody can find where that number comes from.
mission.objective: Make plain terraform apply produce a 45-minute countdown for Pad Delta with holds at T-20 and T-5, taking the values from terraform.tfvars. No other variable file may override them.

mission.name: Trailing Comma At The Arena
mission.description: The Neon Rift laser tag arena receives its configuration as terraform.tfvars.json from the booking system. After a manual edit, Terraform refuses to read it, and after a first fix it complains again.
mission.objective: Make plain terraform apply read terraform.tfvars.json: valid JSON, and the site given as an object with lat and lon. Keep the data in the JSON file (no defaults in the variable blocks).

mission.name: Young Barrel Goes Live
mission.description: Acetaia Bruna's online shop sells whatever the shop_label output says. Last month a 28-day barrel was published as mature because nothing checked the number. The rule exists only as a comment in main.tf.
mission.objective: Add a precondition to the shop_label output so that a plan fails when ageing_days is below min_ageing_days (the default 75 days still publishes, exactly 60 is allowed, and raising the minimum variable raises the bar).

mission.name: Lost In The Enclosure
mission.description: Willowmere Zoo's visitor app reads three outputs out of a nested habitat structure. The data is fine, but each output walks the wrong path through it, and Terraform refuses to validate.
mission.objective: Fix the three outputs so savanna_capacity is 12, aviary_lead_keeper is Mei and reptile_head_keeper is Omar, derived from var.habitats (the check also feeds a different roster).

mission.name: Label That Knows Its Brewery
mission.description: Copperkettle Brewing wants each batch label to default to the brewery name plus -batch, while still allowing special runs to override it. The variable default refers to another variable, and Terraform will not load the file.
mission.objective: Make the label default to Copperkettle-batch and follow the brewery variable (Foxglove-batch for brewery=Foxglove), while an explicit batch_label still overrides it. Keep batch_label as an input variable.

mission.name: Vault Serial Audit
mission.description: Riverside Savings & Trust is being audited. The auditor needs the serial number of the "annex" safe-deposit vault and the codename of the night guard, but nobody wrote them down and the registry file deliberately hides them. They only exist in Terraform's state.
mission.objective: Create the folder answers/ and write two files into it: answers/vault-serial.txt containing the generated serial (the result attribute) of random_integer.serial["annex"], and answers/night-guard.txt containing the id of random_pet.night_guard. Do not change the infrastructure — the plan must stay clean.

mission.name: The Lighthouse Rename
mission.description: The lighthouse roster names tonight's keeper with a random codename that is already printed on badges. A teammate renamed the resource from random_pet.keeper to random_pet.night_keeper, and now terraform plan wants to destroy the codename and generate a new one.
mission.objective: Keep the new name random_pet.night_keeper in the code, keep the existing codename (same ID), and finish with a clean plan. Fix it with a state command — don't add a moved block.

mission.name: Stud Book Handover
mission.description: Meadowbrook Stud's stud book is moving to the regional breeders' association, who will maintain records/stud-book.txt themselves from now on. Our Terraform config still manages that file, so the next cleanup would delete the association's only copy.
mission.objective: Stop managing local_file.stud_book without deleting the file: remove it from the state and from the configuration, keep records/stud-book.txt on disk untouched, keep local_file.vet_log managed, and finish with a clean plan. Use the state CLI, not a removed block.

mission.name: Midnight Kiln Tweak
mission.description: The night technician at a pottery studio hand-edited kiln/firing-schedule.txt on the controller to save a batch of glazes. Terraform did not make that change, and the plan now wants to "create" the schedule file again, which would overwrite the technician's values.
mission.objective: Find out what the technician changed, update the configuration so the schedule describes the values currently on the kiln controller, and end with a clean plan. The file must keep the technician's values; do not revert them.

mission.name: Provenance Fingerprints
mission.description: Hammerstone's authentication desk wants proof that the lot-catalogue state file they were handed is the genuine one. They ask for three fingerprints: the state's serial number, its lineage ID, and the hex value of the lot seal. The raw state JSON has all of them.
mission.objective: Pull the state with terraform state pull and use jq to write answers/serial.txt (the state serial), answers/lineage.txt (the lineage UUID) and answers/seal-hex.txt (the hex attribute of random_id.lot_seal). Change nothing in the infrastructure.

mission.name: Lost Surplus Inventory
mission.description: A tired intern at Redline Army-Surplus Store applied a half-edited branch that had three of the inventory-list resources deleted. Terraform dutifully dropped them from the state, the intern has since restored the code, and the plan now wants to create new manager names, aisle codes and lot numbers, which would invalidate every printed shelf tag.
mission.objective: Bring back the lost state entries so that random_pet.store_manager, random_string.aisle_code and random_integer.lot_number are tracked again with their ORIGINAL values, and the plan is clean. Do not run terraform apply to "fix" it.

mission.name: Orphaned Freezer Tag
mission.description: The Coldharbor vaccine freezer has an asset tag that Terraform generated years ago, but the state that tracked it was lost in a laptop swap. The tag is printed on a sticker, the resource block is still in the code, and the plan wants to generate a different tag and re-label the freezer.
mission.objective: Import the existing tag into random_id.freezer_tag using the terraform import command, with the tag value from inventory/asset-sticker.txt. Afterwards the plan must be clean and the state must hold the original tag. Do not use an import block.

mission.name: Room Sheet Import
mission.description: Warden Ilse wrote an import block to adopt room number the halls already assigned to the first-year student, but terraform plan rejects it. Once the address is sorted out, the plan still wants to throw the number away and draw a fresh one.
mission.objective: Fix imports.tf so the import block adopts the real room number into random_integer.room_number (the number and range are on halls/room-sheet.txt), then run apply so it is imported. The state must hold the original number and the plan must be clean.

mission.name: Robot Controller Roster
mission.description: The Ferrous Bay robot warehouse runs three controller credentials that were created by hand and are now listed in import blocks (imports.tf). Nobody has written the matching resource blocks, and the warehouse's lint rules are strict about how the final config must look.
mission.objective: Let Terraform draft the resource blocks with plan -generate-config-out, then tidy them into main.tf following the team rules in main.tf (all resources in main.tf only, no null-valued attributes, no generator marker comments), and apply so the three objects are imported with their original values. The final plan must be clean.

mission.name: Renamed Zip Passes
mission.description: At Splashdown Treetop Adventure Park a refactor renamed two resources to match the new naming scheme: the climb-pass code and the harness sign. Terraform now plans to destroy both and issue new codes, but the codes are already on sold harness tags.
mission.objective: Keep the new names random_id.climb_pass and local_file.harness_sign, and record the renames in the configuration with moved blocks so the existing objects (same IDs) are kept. Apply, and finish with a clean plan. Do not use the terraform state mv command.

mission.name: Night Market Handoff
mission.description: The Lantern Lane night market is handing its stall permit book to the city clerk, who will keep editing permits/permit-book.txt in her own system. Our configuration still owns the file; deleting the block would make Terraform delete the clerk's working copy.
mission.objective: Stop managing local_file.permit_book with a removed block that has destroy = false, delete the resource block, apply, and keep permits/permit-book.txt on disk. local_file.stall_map stays managed and the plan ends clean. Do not use terraform state rm.

mission.name: Stale Bean Lock
mission.description: The Ember Lane bean catalog module was bumped to require the random provider ~> 3.6 for a new feature, but the committed .terraform.lock.hcl still pins version 3.5.1 from last year. terraform init refuses to continue, and the catalog cannot be generated.
mission.objective: Make terraform init succeed with the constraint ~> 3.6 left in terraform.tf, so that the lock file records a 3.6+ version of hashicorp/random, and apply the configuration so the output catalog_ref exists.

mission.name: Ghost Tuk-Tuk State
mission.description: After a repository reshuffle the Sunrise Tuk-Tuk Tours timetable config points its local backend at a state file that does not exist, so Terraform believes nothing has ever been built. The real production state is sitting in the states/ folder, and a plan now wants to create a second tuk-tuk with a different name.
mission.objective: Point backend "local" at the existing production state file under states/ (the one that holds the tuk-tuk), re-initialise the backend without creating a new state, and end with a clean plan that keeps the original tuk-tuk name and departure minute.

mission.name: Kiosk State Relocation
mission.description: The Lakeland tourist-information kiosk network's state has lived in state/kiosks.tfstate since day one. The new repository layout keeps secrets-adjacent files in vault/, so the backend block already points at vault/kiosks-prod.tfstate, and terraform now refuses to run because the backend changed.
mission.objective: Move the existing state to the new path declared in terraform.tf so it holds the original kiosk serial and refresh interval, with no resources recreated, and finish with a clean plan. Keep the backend path in terraform.tf as it is.

mission.name: Signal Tower Backend
mission.description: Every radio station of the Highland network shares one Terraform config; the state location is supplied per station through a backend config file. The Signal Tower's file config/backend-prod.hcl was written from memory and init rejects it, so the tower has been running on a throwaway default state.
mission.objective: Make the backend use state/signal-tower.tfstate by fixing config/backend-prod.hcl and initialising with -backend-config. Keep the backend block in terraform.tf partial (no path in the .tf files). Then apply so the state file at that path holds the tower's resources.

mission.name: Route Chart First
mission.description: Meridian Haulage's dispatch config has three parts. Tonight the transport manager only needs the route chart published. The load manifest is blocked until weighbridge delivers a ticket file, and a full apply fails on that. A plain terraform apply is useless right now.
mission.objective: Apply only the route chart with -target, so that local_file.route_chart and the route code it depends on exist, while random_pet.driver, local_file.load_manifest and out/load-manifest.txt do not. Leave the configuration (including the weighbridge precondition) untouched.

mission.name: Velvet Door Codes
mission.description: Club Velvet generates door codes with Terraform, one per entrance. A bartender texted the DJ booth code to a friend, so that single code must be regenerated tonight, while the main door, VIP and cloakroom codes stay valid on the printed staff cards.
mission.objective: Regenerate only random_integer.door_code["dj"] using a Terraform CLI option, so its value changes while the other three codes stay exactly as they were. Do not change the code, and finish with a clean plan.

mission.name: Tainted Signing Key
mission.description: A release engineer at Brightwave Firmware tainted the signing key during a scare, then discovered the alarm was false. The key has already been baked into the device bootloaders, yet the plan now wants to destroy it and generate a new one that no device would trust.
mission.objective: Clear the taint on tls_private_key.firmware_signer so Terraform keeps the existing key (same fingerprint) and the plan is clean. Nothing may be replaced.

mission.name: Legacy Orchard Tags
mission.description: Greenfield Orchard's crate-tagging project was last applied years ago with Terraform 0.12. Its state still records the random provider under the pre-0.13 address registry.terraform.io/-/random. Modern Terraform refuses to read it, and a fresh start would reissue every crate tag.
mission.objective: Rewrite the provider address in the existing state to registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/random using the state CLI, so the original crate tag and pallet count survive, terraform init and plan work again, and the plan is clean.

mission.name: Grain Co-op Triage
mission.description: The Three Rivers grain co-op's Terraform state is a mess after a hectic harvest. One resource was renamed in code, another was dropped from the state by accident, and a third was deleted from the code but its log file must be kept for the auditors. The plan wants to destroy and re-draw things that are in daily use.
mission.objective: Reconcile state and code with the state CLI only: keep the renamed random_pet.combine_operator (same name as before), re-adopt random_integer.silo_number with its original value from plates/silo-plate.txt, and forget the retired gauge log without deleting gauges/retired-gauge-log.txt. The final plan must be clean. No moved, import or removed blocks.

mission.name: Ridgeway Route Cards
mission.description: The Ridgeway Rickshaw Charity Rally prints one line per rider from a single format() call. The cards for the 21.1 km rider will not even render, and a recent edit left the tag number padded with spaces instead of zeros.
mission.objective: Make the card for Ines read: TAG-00007 | "Ines \"Flash\" Okafor" | 021.1 km | pace 4:51 min/km (name quoted and escaped, distance zero-padded to width 5 with one decimal). It must still work for any rider object.

mission.name: Ashdown Admission Board
mission.description: The gate office at Ashdown Steam Fair Showground builds its price board with formatlist(), one line per ticket type. Since someone pasted a hand-typed currency list into the call, terraform plan refuses to run at all.
mission.objective: Make price_lines read Weekend Pass — GBP 45.00, Day Ticket — GBP 30.00, Evening Entry — GBP 18.50 for the defaults, using the single currency variable, and still work when there are more tiers.

mission.name: Cinder Lane Serial Tags
mission.description: The repair bench at Cinder Lane prints tags from messy intake notes. Nothing errors, but the printed serial still has punctuation, the fault note keeps its gaps, and the date is still the American-style ISO string.
mission.objective: Make the tag show serial ZX4411B09, the note "Tape loader failing, border flickers on boot" and the date 17/03/2026 for the default inputs, by fixing the three replace() calls so they work for any input.

mission.name: Waymark Pilgrim Trails
mission.description: The Waymark Society's volunteers type each pilgrim trail's waypoints as one comma-separated string. The printed signposts count a blank stop on the Quiet Loop and show stray spaces and double arrows on Heron Way.
mission.objective: Parse each string into clean waypoint names: Heron Way has 3 stops (Oak Gate → Mill Ford → Stone Cross) and the Quiet Loop has 0 and reads closed for walkers. It must hold for other strings too.

mission.name: Kallavik Core Depths
mission.description: Kallavik Ice Station logs ice-core sample depths per drill site. The summary script calls max() and min() with a list, and terraform plan complains about the wrong type for the numbers parameter.
mission.objective: Report the deepest (90.25 m) and shallowest (7.75 m) sample over all sites, their span (82.5 m), and the deepest sample of each site, computed from var.cores.

mission.name: Hollin Diet Whiteboard
mission.description: The cooks' diet whiteboard at Hollin Farm Hospital Kitchen is generated from a batch-size table. When the dietitian added low_salt and gluten_free to the diet list, plan started failing because they have no tailored batch size.
mission.objective: Give listed diets their own batch size and every other diet the standard batch size from var.standard_batch_kg (low_salt 3 kg and gluten_free 3 kg by default), with no hard-coded number.

mission.name: Bell Tower Peal Order
mission.description: At St Aldhelm's the ringing master names the bell to start on, and a script rotates the tower order to match. This week's sheet names Michael, who is not in the tower, and plan refuses to run.
mission.objective: Rotate the bell list so it starts at the named bell. If the name is not in the tower, ring in tower order from the first bell (start_index 0). It must work for any list of bells.

mission.name: Roxy Bout Stubs
mission.description: The Roxy Boxing Club prints one ticket stub per bout, driven by a programme that lists the bouts for each ring. The nested loop that builds the bouts gives Terraform a list of lists, and for_each cannot make sense of it.
mission.objective: Produce a flat list of bouts (ring + bout) and one local_file stub per bout, keyed "<ring>/<bout>": six stubs for the default programme, correct for any programme.

mission.name: Tansy and Tin Pack Labels
mission.description: Tansy & Tin print pack labels by layering each blend's details over the house label and adding the blend's allergens to the house warnings. Right now plan fails on the allergen line, and the label would show the house grade even when the blend has its own.
mission.objective: Layer the blend label over the house label (blend wins), and combine the allergen lists house-first without repeats. Defaults must yield grade BOP, pack 100g pouch and allergens nuts, sesame, soy.

mission.name: Caerwen Robe Roll
mission.description: The Caerwen Choral Society keeps hand-typed sign-up sheets for the concert, the rehearsal and the robe cupboard. Their roll-call script prints doubled names, lists the wrong people for robes, and calls everyone a regular.
mission.objective: Compute everyone (each singer once), regulars (on both the concert and rehearsal sheets) and need_a_robe (concert singers without a robe), using set functions. Defaults give Anwen, Bryn and Rhys as the ones needing robes.

mission.name: Kittiwake Crew Roster
mission.description: Submarine Kittiwake generates its crew roster by decoding config.yaml. Plan complains about a missing attribute, and once that is sorted out the roster shows manual 2.1 instead of 2.10 and a Norwegian interface language of false.
mission.objective: Make the roster read Okonkwo manual 2.10 lang no, Reyes manual 1.8 lang en, Lindqvist manual 3.0 lang off, with the boat name Kittiwake and 2 crew members on watch. The Terraform code must still use yamldecode(file(...)) and work for other config files.

mission.name: Dunmore Telegram Form
mission.description: The Dunmore Telegraph Office renders every outgoing telegram from telegram.tpl. After a tidy-up of the variable names, Terraform stops on the first placeholder and says the template's vars map does not contain a key.
mission.objective: Render the telegram so the file reads STATION: DUNMORE, TO: Capt. Hale, Harbour Master, FROM: Office of the Postmaster, WORDS: 8, a --- line, then the body. It must be driven by the variables, with the template still a separate file.

mission.name: Corvane Estate Address Plan
mission.description: The Corvane Business Park carves its 10.77.0.0/22 range into one equally-sized block per zone with cidrsubnet(). With six zones, plan fails part way through the list claiming the subnet number does not fit.
mission.objective: Give every zone a /26 block taken in order from the base range (gatehouse 10.77.0.0/26, offices 10.77.0.64/26, ...), but derive the newbits from var.subnet_prefix and var.base_cidr so other ranges, prefixes and zone counts work too.

mission.name: Brightside Cubing Results
mission.description: Judges at the Brightside Speedcubing Open type solve times by hand: some use a decimal comma, some leave a space in front, and cubers who did not finish write DNF or DSQ. The results script converts every entry with tonumber() and plan dies on the first one it cannot read.
mission.objective: Convert the times to numbers (13,1 means 13.1, a leading space is ignored), keep only cubers with a numeric time in finishers, list the rest in no_time, and report the winner (Noor, 11.9 s). It must work for other raw_times maps.

mission.name: Tarn Hollow Ride Pass
mission.description: The ride-pass desk at Tarn Hollow decides which zip lines run and the price with two ternary expressions. One of them is rejected by plan for mixing a list with a string, and the other would turn the discount into text for junior guests and break the price for adults.
mission.objective: Make zips always a list (canopy, gorge, valley in peak season, canopy otherwise) and discount_factor always a number (0.5 for juniors, 1 otherwise) so price_eur is a number for every combination of the two flags.

mission.name: Wickham Jar Labels
mission.description: Wickham Candle Works builds its jar labels and pouring sheet with for expressions. Plan fails with an invalid operand while numbering the jars, and then complains about a variable that does not exist while writing the pouring sheet.
mission.objective: Number the jars from 01 in list order with upper-case scents (01-LAVENDER, 02-CEDAR, 03-FIG & HONEY), write one 'scent: grams g' line per batch, and total the wax at 1350 g. All derived from the variables.

mission.name: Kaiten Corner Belts
mission.description: Kaiten Corner sushi bar groups its plates by conveyor belt to print one belt board per belt. Plan fails with a duplicate key as soon as two plates share a belt.
mission.objective: Build by_belt so each belt maps to the list of its plates in serving order (B1: TUNA-1, TUNA-2, TUNA-3; B2: EEL-1, EEL-2; B3: ROE-1) and create exactly one board file per belt.

mission.name: Cinder Valley Watch Roster
mission.description: Cinder Valley Fire Service filters its lookout towers with a for expression: staffed and tall enough for tonight's roster. The roster comes out completely empty, and nobody on the crew can say why.
mission.objective: Keep staffed towers whose height is at least var.min_height_m (25 m): Raven Knob, Tamarack and Grey Rock, in that order. A tower exactly at the minimum counts.

mission.name: Orchard Marionette Programme
mission.description: The Little Orchard Marionette Theatre prints programme notes from three inputs: a cast map keyed by role, a crew list and an optional understudy. The splat expressions on the crew and understudy behave, but the ones on the cast map make plan fail with an unsupported attribute.
mission.objective: Report each puppeteer once in role-key order (Odile, Bram), the crew names, the understudy list (empty when there is none), and the total number of strings (30), keeping splat only where it is appropriate.

mission.name: Nightjar Sleeper Manifest
mission.description: The Nightjar Express prints its sleeper-car manifest from a template string with a %{ for } loop and %{ if } directives. Every directive leaves a blank line behind, so the conductor's sheet is full of gaps.
mission.objective: Make the manifest render exactly: the header line, Berths:, one '  <berth>  <name>' line per passenger with ' (breakfast)' appended where booked, then 'Total: N' with no blank lines (and 'No passengers tonight.' for an empty train).

mission.name: Tarndale Clip Labels
mission.description: The Tarndale wool shearing shed stamps a grade label on every clip through a small module kept in modules/grader. A tidy-up commit moved the module call into the root configuration, and now terraform init refuses to even start.
mission.objective: Make the module call named "grading" find the module that lives in modules/grader, so that terraform apply writes labels/tarndale-summer.txt and the label_file output points at it. The module must stay a separate module (keep module.grading).

mission.name: Lockgate Toll Ledger
mission.description: The keeper of the Willowbrook lock computes boat tolls with a module called lockgate. After a refactor the root configuration calls it with only some of its inputs, and terraform plan stops with a complaint about a missing argument.
mission.objective: Make the lockgate call complete so the module computes the toll from the root variables vessel_beam_m and vessel_length_m. With the defaults the toll_pence output must be 8500, and changing either variable must change the toll. Do not give the module's inputs default values.

mission.name: Gust Gauge Verdict
mission.description: The Skagen kite festival decides each morning which kites may fly from a list of gust readings. The operator types the readings into one variable as comma-separated text, and the windcheck module now rejects that value with a type error.
mission.objective: Keep the root variable gusts as a comma-separated string, and make the windcheck module receive it as the list of numbers it expects. With the default readings the verdict output must be "fly all kites"; with -var gusts="15,40" it must be "stunt kites only".

mission.name: Mycelium Batch Cards
mission.description: The Hollowpine mushroom farm tags every grow room through a module called cellar, which exposes a batch id, a humidity target and the path of the printed tray card. The root configuration that reports them keeps tripping over names that the module does not have.
mission.objective: Make the root configuration read the module's real outputs, so that the root outputs batch, humidity and card show SHI-W14, 78 and ./cards/shiitake.txt with the defaults. They must follow the species and week variables when those change. Do not edit the module.

mission.name: Town Crier Call Roster
mission.description: Master Aldous, the town crier, keeps his call roster in a module called crier. The town hall's root configuration already reports the next call and the roster file, but the module never hands those values out, so every plan ends in an unsupported-attribute error.
mission.objective: Let the module expose what the root configuration asks for, without rewriting the root references. With the default hour 14 the next_call output must be 15:00 and roster_file must be ./calls/master-aldous.txt; with -var hour=23 the next call must be 00:00.

mission.name: Paper Crane Pattern Book
mission.description: The Hinoki origami club prints fold instructions through a module kept in the same repository. A newcomer added a version argument to the module call "to be safe", and now terraform init rejects the whole configuration.
mission.objective: Make the call to the local module work again, keeping source ./modules/folds. With the default model crane, models/crane.txt must list 6 steps and the steps output must be 6; with -var model=frog the steps output must be 4.

mission.name: Boardwalk Lamp Posts
mission.description: The Brightwater boardwalk numbers its lamp posts through a module that is instantiated once per post with count. The first attempt stamps the same number on every post, and the outputs that report the posts refuse to compile.
mission.objective: Create posts_total instances of module.post, numbered starting from 1 (labels LP-01, LP-02, ...), and make the labels output the list of all labels and last_label the label of the final post. With the default of 3 posts labels is LP-01, LP-02, LP-03; with -var posts_total=5 it has five entries.

mission.name: Glassblowers' Kiln Board
mission.description: Ember Row Glass anneals every piece in its own kiln module instance, one per kind of ware. The studio manager's attempt to build the instances from a plain list is rejected, and the board that should show the vase's annealing time looks the vase up under the wrong key.
mission.objective: Create one module.piece instance per entry of the pieces list, addressed by name, and make vase_hours the vase's annealing time. With the defaults kiln/schedule.txt must read bowl:6h, ornament:4h, vase:10h (one per line, sorted by name) and vase_hours must be 10.

mission.name: Zamboni Waits For Ice
mission.description: At the Northgate ice rink, a chiller module lays down the ice and writes an ice log, and a resurfacer module reads that log to schedule the next resurfacing. On a fresh checkout the plan dies because the log does not exist yet, and after a thickness change the schedule lags one apply behind.
mission.objective: Make module.resurfacer wait for module.chiller with an explicit dependency. After one apply from scratch resurface_after_min must be 50 (twice the ice thickness of 25 mm), and after a single apply with -var thickness_mm=30 it must be 60.

mission.name: Wexcombe Offsite Ledger
mission.description: The Wexcombe tapestry atelier records every restoration treatment twice: once with its primary provider and once with the aliased "offsite" provider. The ledger module was written to expect a second provider configuration, and the root configuration never hands one over.
mission.objective: Give module.ledger both provider configurations: the default local provider for its primary copy and the aliased local.offsite for its mirror copy. State must record module.ledger.local_file.mirror as managed by the offsite provider configuration.

mission.name: Hollow Lane Audio Guide
mission.description: The Hollow Lane ghost walk company generates audio-guide scripts from a template that ships inside the guide module. Since the module was extracted, the scripts land in the wrong folder, and the template cannot be found at all.
mission.objective: Make module.guide read its template from its own directory and write the finished script into the root workspace: audio/haunted-cellar.txt (not inside modules/guide). The audio_file output must be ./audio/haunted-cellar.txt and the script must greet walkers of the stop named in the variable.

mission.name: Escape Room Door Code
mission.description: The Cipher Cellar escape room draws a fresh door code for every booking in a module called room. The code is generated as a secret, and Terraform now refuses to plan because the root output passes it along without admitting that it is sensitive, and the module itself never documents that its output is a secret.
mission.objective: Make the secret door code flow from module.room to the root output door_code with sensitivity declared on both outputs (the module's code and the root's door_code), still generated by random_password. terraform output must show door_code as sensitive; terraform output -raw door_code must print an all-digit code of the length given by code_length (6 by default), and the same code must end up in keys/booking.txt.

mission.name: Gilded Cuff Programme Codes
mission.description: The Gilded Cuff magic show prints a programme line for each production through a module with strict input checks: show codes must look like SOR-07 and doors must open between 15 and 90 minutes before curtain. The caller feeds it raw values and the module's own validation rejects them.
mission.objective: Fix the caller, not the checks. With the defaults (act "sorcerer", run number 7, doors 1 hour early) the programme output must be "SOR-07 | doors 60 min before curtain". Run number 12 must give SOR-12, and a 2-hour doors_open_hours must still be rejected by the module's validation.

mission.name: Balloon Basket Limits
mission.description: Skyward Balloons flies two kinds of trip. A module guards each booking with a precondition so that the sunrise basket carries at most 8 passengers and the standard basket at most 12. Since a refactor the guard turns away perfectly legal bookings and accepts illegal ones.
mission.objective: Repair the precondition inside the module: sunrise flights allow 1 to 8 passengers, standard flights allow 1 to 12, anything else must be rejected by the module's own error message. The default booking (standard, 10 passengers) must apply and write manifest.txt with "standard flight: 10 passengers".

mission.name: Boiler Shed Extraction
mission.description: The Whistling Pennant traction engine club has been issuing its boiler ticket and shed manifest from the root configuration for months. A refactor moved both resources into a module called shed, and plan now wants to destroy the live ticket (printed on the engine's paperwork) and create a new one.
mission.objective: Keep the module and keep the existing ticket: the random_id and the manifest file must end up at module.shed.random_id.ticket and module.shed.local_file.manifest with the same IDs as before, and the plan must be clean. Record the move in the code with moved blocks.

mission.name: Sugarhouse Season Label
mission.description: Hollisford Sugarbush labels its syrup tins through two nested modules: the evaporator takes the sugarbush and season from the root and hands them to the canner, which writes the label. Every label comes out with the right sugarbush but "unknown" as the season.
mission.objective: Thread the season variable all the way down: root, evaporator module, canner module. With the default 2023 the file syrup/hollisford-2023.txt must read "Hollisford Sugarbush syrup, season 2023"; with -var season=2019 the label and the file name must follow, and the label output must stay available at the root.

mission.name: Sauna Supper Menu
mission.description: The Nordlys Lakeside Sauna Retreat prints its evening menu with a module that the kitchen team wrote years ago. The retreat's root configuration uses a current local provider, and terraform init now says that no provider version can satisfy everybody.
mission.objective: Make terraform init succeed with the root's provider requirement (hashicorp/local ~> 2.5) left as it is, by repairing the conflicting requirement declared inside the module. The module must keep declaring the provider it uses. The menu file menu/supper.txt must list the dishes, numbered.

mission.name: Busker Pitch Board
mission.description: The Cobbleway buskers' circuit posts a board for every busker: a JSON record and a list of its fields. The busker module already publishes performer, slot and setlist as outputs. The root configuration tries to use the whole module object as a single value and Terraform rejects both attempts.
mission.objective: Use the entire module.busker object as the value: the board file board/busker.json must contain it as JSON, and the fields output must list the module's output names alphabetically (performer, setlist, slot). Don't type the field names or values out by hand: they must follow the module.

mission.name: Helpline Queue Defaults
mission.description: The Brightwater call centre declares its queues in a map and lets a module fill the gaps: 128 kbps and a hold jingle unless the queue says otherwise. The module's type demands every field, so any queue that omits one is rejected.
mission.objective: Let the module accept queues that omit bitrate_kbps and jingle, defaulting them to 128 and true respectively, while skill stays mandatory. queues/rota.txt must read "billing refunds@128k", "night_desk triage@128k +jingle" and "sales_line upgrades@64k +jingle", one per line.

mission.name: Yoga Room Prep Times
mission.description: The Lotus Lane yoga studio books a room per class style with one module instance each. The coordinator's summary outputs are meant to map each class style to its minutes and to total them, but the splat expressions she used choke on the module instances.
mission.objective: Make prep_minutes a map from class style to prep minutes (5 per student) and total_minutes their sum. With the defaults (vinyasa 12, hatha 9, yin 6, ashtanga 7 students) the map is vinyasa 60, hatha 45, yin 30, ashtanga 35 and the total 170; with -var 'classes={ashtanga=3,hatha=4}' the total must be 35.

mission.name: Same Card Four Times
mission.description: The Blackwood Manor murder mystery dinner prints one card per clue with a counted local_file. On dinner night the cards folder holds a single card, and it always shows the last clue - four resources keep overwriting one file.
mission.objective: Give every counted card its own file, cards/clue-0.txt up to cards/clue-3.txt, by using count.index in the filename. Keep the single counted resource and make sure a longer clue list would produce clue-4.txt.

mission.name: Five Dogs Three Charts
mission.description: The Northgate sled-dog kennel keeps its roster in a variable, but feeding charts are generated by a counted resource whose count someone typed in by hand. Two dogs on the roster have no chart, and the vet is not amused.
mission.objective: Every dog on var.dogs must get a chart (five today, charts/tundra.txt through charts/nome.txt). The chart count must follow the roster - adding or removing a name from var.dogs must add or remove exactly the matching chart.

mission.name: Bay Zero
mission.description: Quayside's multi-storey car park generates a sign per bay. The floor manager walked the deck this morning and found a sign reading BAY 0 and no sign for the last bay number. Terraform counts from zero; drivers do not.
mission.objective: Label the signs 1-based: files signs/bay-01.txt to signs/bay-06.txt with content 'BAY n of 6'. There must be exactly six signs and no bay-00; the number of bays must stay variable.

mission.name: Lights On, Maybe
mission.description: Eastbank skatepark prints a floodlight schedule only on nights when the lights are on. The switch is a variable the caretaker sets to "on", and now the plan refuses to start with a complaint about the condition of a count expression.
mission.objective: Make the floodlights variable a real bool (type = bool) and set it to true in terraform.tfvars, so that one schedule file is created when it is true and none when it is false. Do not compare the variable with a string.

mission.name: One Closure Shown
mission.description: The city film office issues a closure permit per production with a counted resource. The film office's portal reads the closure_paths output and keeps complaining that it receives a single string, with only the first production's permit.
mission.objective: Make closure_paths a list that contains the path of every closure permit, in production order, for any number of shoots - including an empty list when no production applied.

mission.name: Briggs Twice
mission.description: The Lacegate antiques centre prints a price tag per stall, and the stalls are listed in a variable as plain strings. After a refactor from count to for_each, Terraform complains that it cannot iterate over a list of strings - and one dealer appears twice in the list.
mission.objective: Make for_each work on var.dealers so there is exactly one tag per distinct dealer, addressed as local_file.stall_tag["briggs"] and so on (four tags from the default list). Keep var.dealers a list(string).

mission.name: Two Attendants One Card
mission.description: The Marlowe Pier amusement park writes a duty card for every operator from a map of name to role. The cards folder has only three files, one of them called attendant.txt, and the supervisor's card says her name is 'supervisor'.
mission.objective: Write cards/<name>.txt for every operator in var.crew (four files) containing exactly 'Name: <name>' and 'Role: <role>' on two lines. Instances must stay keyed by operator name.

mission.name: Tickets Without Keys
mission.description: The Marrow Lane Literary Festival writes a ticket stub per session with for_each. The box-office app wants an output that maps each event to its ticket file, but the output block errors as soon as Terraform reads it.
mission.objective: Make the ticket_files output a map from event slug to ticket path (three entries today), built from the for_each resource. It must follow whatever sessions the variable holds.

mission.name: Call Sign Chain
mission.description: The Skyward Air Cadets give each cadet a random radio call sign and print it on a wing card. Terraform stops before it plans anything: the wing card refers to 'the' call sign, but there is one call sign per cadet.
mission.objective: Create one local_file.wing_card per cadet, keyed by cadet name, driven by the random_pet.callsign instances themselves (for_each over the resource). Each card must contain its own cadet's call sign and nothing may be regenerated when a cadet joins or leaves.

mission.name: Slot Slips
mission.description: Millbrook food bank schedules pickup slots in a variable of objects: who collects, how many boxes and when. The slip generator tries to print the whole slot object into a string, and Terraform refuses.
mission.objective: Make each slip read exactly 'Slot <name>: <volunteer> collects <boxes> boxes at <time>' (one line, trailing newline), taking the three values from the slot object. Keep for_each over var.slots.

mission.name: Secret Keys
mission.description: Kingsgate's tower-crane operators each get a cab PIN slip, driven by a sensitive map of name to PIN. Terraform refuses to loop over the map: it would have to use secret values as instance keys.
mission.objective: Keep var.pins sensitive and create one local_sensitive_file.pin_slip per operator, keyed by the operator's name (vesna, hamid, lotte), with the file containing exactly that operator's PIN. Do not make the PIN map itself non-sensitive.

mission.name: Zip By Another Name
mission.description: Greystone School bundles each trip's paperwork into one zip with archive_file, generating one entry per document using a dynamic block. Terraform insists the block type does not exist.
mission.objective: Make dist/trip-pack.zip contain one entry for every key of var.documents (consent-form.txt, packing-list.txt, emergency-card.txt) with the matching text, using a dynamic block that produces archive_file's own nested block type.

mission.name: Class Iterator
mission.description: Iron Crane Dojo builds a weekly class zip with a dynamic block. A colleague gave the loop a friendlier iterator name, class, but half the references still use the old one, and Terraform cannot find the variable.
mission.objective: Keep the custom iterator (iterator = class) and make the block read each class's file and text through it, so bundles/week.zip holds the three class files with the right text and follows var.classes.

mission.name: Transcript Optional
mission.description: The Oakridge Sculpture Park ships an audio-guide zip. A large-print transcript is added only when the curator has written one, but the pack builder insists on the transcript entry and fails whenever the variable is left empty.
mission.objective: Build packs/audio-guide.zip with the stops list and guide script always present, and the large- print transcript entry only when var.transcript is not null. With the default (null) the plan must succeed and the zip must have two entries.

mission.name: Every Room Every Day
mission.description: The Nightowl Hackathon books each room for each day, using setproduct to get all the pairs. Terraform rejects the result as a for_each argument.
mission.objective: Create one booking per room and day, addressed local_file.booking["<room>/<day>"] (six today: atrium, garage, loft by fri, sat), with the file bookings/<room>-<day>.txt. Adding a day or room later must only add new bookings.

mission.name: Keys From The Future
mission.description: The Kelpwater marine lab stamps each sample label with the id of the survey run, a random_id. The plan dies on the very first run: Terraform complains that the for_each keys depend on something it only knows after apply.
mission.objective: Make the labels work on a fresh plan: one local_file.label per sample, keyed by the plain sample name (kelp-a, kelp-b, urchin-c), while the file name and text still carry the run id (labels/<sample>-<run id>.txt).

mission.name: Painted On The Hull
mission.description: The Lakeview swan pedalos each have a random mascot name that is already painted on the hulls. Someone converted the mascots from count to for_each so pedalos are identified by name. The state still has them at numeric positions, and the plan wants to replace all three.
mission.objective: Add moved blocks so Terraform moves random_pet.mascot[0], [1] and [2] to their pedalo keys (odette, odile, benno) with the same names - no mascot destroyed or recreated - and finish with a clean plan.

mission.name: Closed Snack Bar
mission.description: Starlight Roller Disco switches its snack-bar module on with count on session nights only. The root outputs read the module's outputs as if it always existed, and Terraform now says the module is a tuple.
mission.objective: Make menu_path and menu_items work in both states: with the snack bar open they show the path (a string) and the item list; with it closed, menu_path is null and menu_items is an empty list. Keep count on the module call.

mission.name: Steelpan Tuning Sheet
mission.description: The tuner at the Calypso Hill steelpan yard keeps each pan's tuning notes in a text file. Terraform is supposed to read the sheet and print a pan card, but the plan dies before a single note is counted.
mission.objective: Make the data source read the real tuning sheet so that output pan_name is "Tenor Lead" and note_count is 29, and out/pan-card.txt is generated from it. The values must keep coming from the sheet, not from the config.

mission.name: Compass Rose Proof
mission.description: The map room copies a binary engraving of the compass rose into a press folder as a proof. It applies cleanly, but every following plan insists the proof has changed and wants to replace it.
mission.objective: Make press/rose-proof.png a byte-for-byte copy of art/compass-rose.png, and make the plan clean after apply. Keep reading the engraving through the data source.

mission.name: Bungee Weigh-In Card
mission.description: Before each session at the gorge bungee platform, a helper script totals the jumpers' weight and Terraform prints the jump card. Since the script was extended with a jump master name and a weight limit, Terraform refuses to read its answer.
mission.objective: Fix the script so the external data source accepts it. Terraform must then output total_kg 303, headroom_kg 57 and the four jumper names, all computed from roster/jumpers.csv.

mission.name: Falconry Weigh-In
mission.description: The mews keeps a script that turns a falcon's body weight into its ideal flying weight. Terraform passes the bird and the numbers to it, but every plan dies with a complaint from the script about a missing query.
mission.objective: Deliver bird, weight_g and target_pct to bin/flying-weight.sh the way the external data source supports. With the defaults, flying_weight_g must be 959 and the weigh-in file must show 61 g to lose. Changing the variables must change the answer.

mission.name: Cave Survey Probes
mission.description: Three probe scripts feed the base-camp board of a cave survey: borehole depth, oxygen and humidity. Terraform cannot start any of them, and each failure has a different cause.
mission.objective: Make all three external data sources run, so the outputs read depth_m 84, o2_pct 19.6 and humidity_pct 97 from survey/readings.txt, and camp/board.txt is written. Keep the data sources and the probe scripts.

mission.name: Formulator's Batch Sheet
mission.description: A cosmetics lab generates a batch sheet with Terraform, then reads the sheet back with a data source to work out how much fragrance oil goes in. On a fresh bench the plan fails because the sheet is not there yet; on a bench that already has one, changing the base weight still gives yesterday's fragrance dose.
mission.objective: Make the data source wait for the batch sheet that this config creates, so a single apply works from nothing and always reflects the current base_grams. With the default 240 g, fragrance_g is 14.4; with base_grams=500 it is 30.

mission.name: Score Folio Contents
mission.description: A sheet music publisher builds the contents page of a songbook from one score file per piece. The score data source uses count, one instance per piece, but the config does not handle its instances correctly and the plan refuses to run.
mission.objective: Make the contents page list every piece in order. With the default list, total_notes is 3580 and piece_titles has three titles; with scores=["p04","p02"] the outputs must follow the new list.

mission.name: Longline Sample Sheets
mission.description: A seaweed farm keeps one sample sheet per longline. Terraform reads every sheet with a single for_each data source and builds the farm board, but the config trips over how for_each names, finds and returns its instances.
mission.objective: Make the data source read samples/*.txt and output growth as a map keyed by longline id without the extension ({"l07-kelp": 23.4, "l12-dulse": 24.1, "l15-kelp": 22.8}), with average_growth "23.43". A sheet added to samples/ must appear automatically.

mission.name: Ranger Snow Patrol
mission.description: Each ranger on the national park's trails leaves a JSON note. A small local module wraps the data source that reads one note and hands back a reading. The root config that calls the module twice cannot find the values it asks for.
mission.objective: Make the root config use what the module really outputs. lowest_snow_cm must be 148 and open_trails must be ["north"]; the patrol log must show both rangers. The data source must stay inside the module.

mission.name: Gritter Depot Handshake
mission.description: The gritting depot team publishes the depot code, bay count and first departure as outputs of their own Terraform configuration, applied in the depot-team folder. The route planning team's data source is supposed to read those facts, but the plan reports that it cannot find any remote state.
mission.objective: Make terraform_remote_state read the depot team's real state so that the routes header says "Depot NGD-04: 6 bays, first gritter 05:12". The values must come from the remote state, not from the config.

mission.name: Ballroom Season Programme
mission.description: The ballroom dance hall's front desk prints its season programme from outputs that the floor-staff team publishes in their own Terraform state. The plan fails because the front desk asks for outputs that are not there, and then treats one of them as the wrong kind of value.
mission.objective: Read the floor staff's real outputs correctly. total_couples must be 160 and head_caller "Wilhelmina Pike", both derived from the remote state, and the programme must list both floors.

mission.name: Tool Library Rota
mission.description: The tool library's stock room keeps a JSON stock register. The weekend rota must list the serviceable tools by class and send the broken ones to the mending corner, but the expression that filters the register does not even evaluate.
mission.objective: Fix the filter so ready_by_class is {"garden": ["T-01","T-04"], "power": ["T-02","T-05"]} and needs_repair is ["T-03"]. The outputs must keep being computed from the register.

mission.name: Banquet Place Cards
mission.description: The caterer's guest list is a JSON export where table numbers and dietary notes are only present for some guests, and sometimes explicitly null. The place-card config crashes as soon as it meets a guest without them.
mission.objective: Print a card for every guest: a missing table becomes "TBA" and a missing or null diet becomes "no restrictions". With the supplied list, special_diets must be 2 and the last card "Ambrose Tull | table TBA | nut allergy".

mission.name: Stamp Sheet Label Receipt
mission.description: The distributor wants the philatelic bureau's stamp-sheet labels as a single zip, with a receipt carrying the bundle's checksum. The archive data source cannot build the bundle, and the distributor's tooling expects a checksum format the receipt does not use.
mission.objective: Build dist/bureau.zip from the labels folder, leaving out the unfinished *.tmp draft labels. bundle_sha256 and the receipt must carry the hex SHA-256 of the zip (the same value shasum -a 256 prints), and bundle_size its size in bytes.

mission.name: Till Room Combination
mission.description: The charity shop's till-room takings safe combination lives in a file on the back-office laptop, and Terraform prints the shift manager's door card from it. Reviewers noticed the combination shows up in plain text in the apply log, in the outputs, and in a card anybody on the machine can read.
mission.objective: Read the combination with the data source made for secrets, keep it out of plan, apply and output display (the combination output must be marked sensitive and still return the real value on request), and make tillroom/door-card.txt readable by its owner only (0600).

mission.name: Groundsman On The Wrong Ground
mission.description: Willowbank cricket ground writes its pitch-preparation plan per environment, with a workspace each for staging and prod. A trainee ran terraform apply while the CLI was still sitting in the default workspace, so the staging plan was never created where it belongs.
mission.objective: Make the staging workspace the selected one and have the pitch preparation plan applied there: out/staging-groundsman-plan.txt must exist and be tracked in staging's own state, the plan must be clean, and the prod workspace must stay empty.

mission.name: Lavender Crate Labels
mission.description: Brackenfield Lavender Farm keeps one workspace per harvest, such as midsummer or late-bloom. The crate manifest is meant to be named after the harvest, but the files and labels come out stamped with the literal text of the expression instead of the workspace name.
