mission.objective: In a workspace named midsummer, Terraform must write out/midsummer-crates.txt whose first line is 'Harvest: midsummer', and the output crate_label must be 'midsummer-3'. The same config must work for any workspace name.

mission.name: The Silent Pager
mission.description: The Saltmarsh fish hatchery pages a human on call only in production, with 90-day tank logs and a pager roster. Since the last deploy prod behaves like a dev sandbox: logs are kept for a week and nobody gets paged, although the prod workspace is selected.
mission.objective: In the workspace named prod the output retention_days must be 90, pager_enabled must be true and out/pager-roster.txt must exist. Every other workspace (dev, staging ...) keeps retention 7 with no pager.

mission.name: Hut Count Missing
mission.description: The seafront beach hut rental lays out its huts from a settings map keyed by workspace. Dev and prod have entries, but the new qa workspace, created for the staff dry run, stops every plan with an indexing error.
mission.objective: Make the config work in the qa workspace with 12 huts, hours 09-16 and no towels, while dev (4 huts, 10-14, no towels) and prod (24 huts, 08-18, towels) keep their values. The settings must still be looked up by terraform.workspace.

mission.name: The Unwatched Fountain
mission.description: Each fountain in the Marlow city fountains network has its own workspace. The spray schedule must never be applied in the nameless default workspace, so someone added a guard. It prints a polite warning in default and then carries on creating files.
mission.objective: Applying in the default workspace must fail and write nothing, with an error rather than a warning. In any named workspace, such as fountain-a or fountain-b, the apply must still succeed and write out/<workspace>-sprays.txt.

mission.name: The Misfiled Bauble State
mission.description: Tinsel Lane Christmas decorations factory keeps one workspace per season and uses the local backend. During a laptop migration somebody dragged the winter workspace's state file out of its folder. Terraform now thinks winter is empty and wants to rebuild the whole bauble log.
mission.objective: Make the winter workspace (selected) own its original state again, in the exact location the local backend reads, and leave the summer workspace alone. No stray state files may remain in terraform.tfstate.d/ and the plan must be clean.

mission.name: Bunks Over Bunks
mission.description: Pinewater youth summer camp runs an east and a west wing, one workspace each. Both wings write their bunk roster and wake-up list to the same two files, so whichever wing applied last wins and the other wing's plan shows endless drift.
mission.objective: Give each workspace its own bunk roster and wake-up list: after applying in both east and west, each wing's files must exist separately, mention only their own wing, and a plan in either wing must be clean.

mission.name: Relay Perches
mission.description: A pigeon-post network keeps one perch card per relay station. The pilot workspace runs two stations and the network workspace runs every station, each with its own list in a locals map. The plan refuses to expand the list into resources.
mission.objective: In the pilot workspace there must be exactly two local_file.perch instances and in the network workspace exactly four, keyed by station slug (elm-hill, dovecote, mill-pond, ash-cross). The output station_count must match.

mission.name: Strike Zone Overflow
mission.description: The Rolling Thunder bowling alley builds its lane sheets with a small module whose lane count comes from the workspace: four for prod, two for staging. When a developer opened a throwaway workspace for pull request 142, the module rejected the run before a single lane was created.
mission.objective: Keep 4 lanes in prod and 2 in staging, and give every other workspace (such as pr-142 or hotfix-7) exactly 1 lane, without weakening the module's own input validation.

mission.name: Retiring The Trial Batch
mission.description: Willow Bend handmade paper mill spun up a workspace called trial for an experimental pulp recipe, and it is now retired. A volunteer's attempt to delete the workspace was refused, and the mill does not want orphaned files left in out/.
mission.objective: Remove the trial workspace entirely, with its resources destroyed first so that out/trial- batch.txt is gone, while the keep workspace and its batch file stay untouched.

mission.name: Rehearsal Jam Kitchen
mission.description: The Bramble Lane jam kitchen named its seasonal batch with a random codename and stored a snapshot of that state in snapshots/jam-ledger.tfstate. The staff want a workspace called rehearsal that begins with that same batch, not a brand new codename.
mission.objective: Create the workspace rehearsal seeded from snapshots/jam-ledger.tfstate: it must be selected, hold the original batch codename from the snapshot, and show a clean plan. Do not change the configuration.

mission.name: Wheel Profiles
mission.description: Pinewood Ferris Wheel Hire keeps one YAML settings file per environment in env/, chosen by workspace name. In the dev workspace the build dies complaining about an attribute on a string, and in prod there is no settings file for the workspace at all.
mission.objective: In workspaces dev, staging and prod the config must load env/<workspace>.yaml and write out/<workspace>-wheel.conf. The outputs rotation and pod_count must be 412.5/12 for dev, 540.5/24 for staging and 725.5/36 for prod.

mission.name: Photo Booth Price Table
mission.description: The Eastgate photo-booth kiosk keeps its pricing formula in Terraform and a colleague who normally writes pytest added a test file for it. Running terraform test refuses to even start, complaining about the blocks in tests/prices.tftest.hcl.
mission.objective: Make terraform test run and pass all three scenarios (single_print, three_prints, discount_half) in tests/prices.tftest.hcl without removing any of them or weakening what they assert.

mission.name: Colour Formula On Disk
mission.description: A hair salon generates its colour formula card with Terraform. The test that proves the card really lands on disk fails every time, even though terraform apply writes the file just fine.
mission.objective: Make all three runs in tests/colour.tftest.hcl pass (formula_file_written, total_for_default_batch, bigger_batch) while still checking that salon/formula.txt exists and lists pigment at 800 g.

mission.name: Orienteering Cutoff Logic
mission.description: The Saltmere orienteering club's pacing sheet is generated by Terraform and its checks are written in a test file. Three assertions fail on a configuration that is behaving correctly: the error messages describe the right intent, but the conditions say the opposite.
mission.objective: Fix the condition expressions in tests/pacing.tftest.hcl so every run passes, keeping all four asserts and their error messages. The code in pacing.tf is correct and must not change.

mission.name: Rook Club Pairings
mission.description: The Rook and Pawn chess club generates tournament boards with a small module that has two required inputs and no defaults. Its test file tries to supply them once at the top, but Terraform will not even load the file.
mission.objective: Fix tests/pairings.tftest.hcl so both runs pass, supplying club and players through a single file-level variables block that the runs share, with the second run overriding only players.

mission.name: Dispensary Label Guardrails
mission.description: A pharmacy label generator refuses dangerous doses with variable validation, and two tests are supposed to prove it. Both report that the validation fired - and still fail, one complaining that an expected failure never happened.
mission.objective: Make dose_too_high and interval_too_short pass by pointing expect_failures at the right variable address in each run, without touching the validation rules in label.tf.

mission.name: Overstocked Henhouse
mission.description: A poultry farm sizes its coops with a little Terraform module: square feet of floor per hen and an overstocked flag. The crowded-coop scenarios in the test file never get a chance to run - Terraform rejects the values they try to override.
mission.objective: Correct the per-run variable overrides in tests/coop.tftest.hcl so that all three runs pass: the type of each override must match the declared variable, and the assertions must stay unchanged.

mission.name: Sailmaker Cutting Order
mission.description: A sail loft calculates the area of a mainsail, then orders cloth with a 10 percent waste allowance based on that measured area. The test file chains the two steps with run outputs, but Terraform reports a dependency cycle before a single run starts.
mission.objective: Fix tests/sailloft.tftest.hcl so measure_main, order_cloth and spare_jib all pass, with order_cloth consuming run.measure_main.sail_area and spare_jib comparing against run.order_cloth.

mission.name: Unmixed Paint Batch
mission.description: A paint shop stamps every tin with a random batch code and a random tint shade. The tests that check the stamps fail with "Unknown condition value" even though nothing is wrong with the codes themselves.
mission.objective: Make ratio_label, batch_code_shape and tint_in_range pass. Keep ratio_label as a plan-only run, and keep the regex and range assertions; the runs that read random values must be able to see them.

mission.name: Window Crew Dispatch Mock
mission.description: A window-cleaning company stamps every job with a random ticket and a random dispatch zone. To test the stamp format deterministically the team wrapped the random provider in a mock, but the mock either fails to load or hands out random values anyway.
mission.objective: Repair the mock_provider "random" block in tests/dispatch.tftest.hcl so that mocked values reach the outputs: ticket WC-AB12CD34 and zone-4. All three runs must pass without removing the mock.

mission.name: Snow Globe Overrides
mission.description: A snow globe assembly workshop prints a work ticket from two random choices: an assembly station and the number of glitter scoops to add to each globe. The tests override both random resources to fixed values, but Terraform prints warnings about override targets and the assertions see random numbers.
mission.objective: Correct the override_resource target addresses in tests/ticket.tftest.hcl (including the one inside the glitter module) so that ticket_default sees station-3/scoops-8, ticket_reprinted sees the same ticket, and terraform test finishes without any "Invalid override target" warning.

mission.name: Disc Golf Wind Check
mission.description: Terraform decides whether the disc golf course may open for play by reading the wind meter's output file. That file only exists on the course, so the tests have to fake the reading with override_data, and two of the three scenarios cannot read it.
mission.objective: Make calm_morning, gale_warning and gusty_edge pass using override_data on data.local_file.windmeter in each run (values must set the real attribute that the code reads). Do not create sensor/wind-kph.txt.

mission.name: Mosaic Panel Modules
mission.description: The harbourside tile mosaic guild keeps two small helper modules, one for tiles and one for the frieze, and a panel order that combines them. Two test runs are meant to exercise the helpers directly but cannot find them.
mission.objective: Make tile_area, frieze_area and panel_total pass: each module run must point at the helper module's real directory, and the tests must keep checking 3468 cm2 for tiles and 7400 cm2 for the frieze.

mission.name: Storage Unit Lock Codes
mission.description: A self-storage company issues each unit a random numeric lock code and keeps it in a sensitive output. The test for the code policy fails, but every failure message is just "(sensitive value)", so nobody can tell what is actually wrong.
mission.objective: Make code_policy and public_label pass without ever unmasking the lock code itself: the policy is an 8-digit numeric code, the unit label is "Unit A-14". The output must stay sensitive and the test must not contain nonsensitive(output.lock_code).

mission.name: Mint Press Room
mission.description: A small coin mint's Terraform writes a strike sheet through a "press" provider alias and a read-only die log through a "vault" alias. The test file configures providers of its own, and one alias is not the one the code expects.
mission.objective: Make sheet_goes_to_press, die_is_read_only and series_number_flows pass by giving the test file provider blocks for exactly the aliases the configuration requires (press and vault), and map them in the runs that pass providers explicitly.

mission.name: Comedy Club Lineup Setup
mission.description: A stand-up comedy club computes whether a show needs an intermission from an act lineup file. The tests use a helper module to write that lineup before the real tests read it, but neither helper step does its job.
mission.objective: Make setup, short_show, setup_long and double_header pass: both helper runs must really apply tests/setup and feed their lineup_path output to the run that follows. No lineup may be left behind after terraform test.

mission.name: Climbing Wall Route Card
mission.description: A climbing gym generates a route card for every wall route: grade, hold colour, number of bolts and whether a top rope is allowed. The test for the card is one long && assertion that fails with the message "route card is wrong", which tells setters nothing.
mission.objective: Split the compound asserts in tests/routes.tftest.hcl into separate asserts, one per fact, each with its own specific error_message and no && in any condition. Then use the failing one to find and fix the real defect: a 17 m route needs 9 bolts.

mission.name: Concours Stand Cards
mission.description: Every car entered in the Quayside classic car concours gets a stand card generated from a map of entries. The tests try to inspect individual cards but address them as if the cards were a numbered list, and Terraform rejects every one of them.
mission.objective: Fix the instance addresses in tests/concours.tftest.hcl so that arrow_card, regent_card and all_cards_issued pass, addressing the for_each instances by key. The three-entry check and the stand text must stay.

mission.name: Fireworks Display Permit
mission.description: The county fireworks permit office issues display permits through Terraform, and two preconditions on the permit resource refuse displays that carry too much explosive or stack their racks too tall. The negative tests meant to prove that the refusals work report failures of their own.
mission.objective: Make within_limits, too_heavy and too_tall pass, with each negative run using expect_failures on the object that really holds the precondition and a variable override that really violates exactly that rule.

mission.name: Whisper Down The Cable
mission.description: The Brest cable-landing station opens its uplink with a handshake script that Terraform starts through local-exec. A security reviewer ran ps during an apply and read the station password in the process list.
mission.objective: Keep calling bin/handshake.sh with --site brest-landing, but stop putting the password in the command line. The script must receive it in its environment as LANDING_PASSWORD, with the variable staying sensitive.

mission.name: Seals Of The Salt Road
mission.description: A caravan company issues one wax-seal token per trading post and keeps each in a file. The ledger config sensitive-marks the whole post-to-token map, and Terraform refuses to plan, complaining about for_each and about an output that was derived from the secrets.
mission.objective: Make the config apply: a plain set variable post_names (default petra, merv, palmyra) drives for_each, a sensitive map variable seal_tokens supplies each token, post_count is 3, and seal_digests (sha256 of each token) is a sensitive output. Do not use nonsensitive().

mission.name: Frost Alarm Sunshine
mission.description: A cranberry bog arms its frost alarm with a code that Terraform writes onto a panel file the whole harvest crew can read. Someone wanted the crew to see the code loaded, wrapped it in nonsensitive(), and the code now prints in every plan.
mission.objective: Stop revealing alarm_code: the panel file and every plan or apply must not contain it, output alarm_code must be sensitive but still carry the real value, and output code_length must stay a plain, non-sensitive number equal to the code's length (shown on the panel as 'Code length: N characters').

mission.name: Box Office Keys In Git
mission.description: The Harbourside Brass band sells tickets through a payment gateway whose API key was typed into terraform.tfvars next to the ticket price, and terraform.tfvars is committed to the shared repo. The treasurer has asked for the key to rotate and for it never to appear in the repository again.
mission.objective: Remove the gateway key from every .tf and .tfvars file (keep band_name and ticket_price_pence in terraform.tfvars). The key must be supplied from outside the repo through the TF_VAR_gateway_api_key environment variable, still ending up mode 0600 in box-office/gateway.env.

mission.name: Wrong Name On The Armoury Door
mission.description: A fencing club's CI job exports TF_VAR_armoury_code, TF_VAR_club_region and TF_VAR_squad_roster before it runs Terraform, yet the keypad code and the region never arrive. The pipeline keeps stopping on missing values that the engineers swear they set.
mission.objective: Make the variable names match what the CI job exports: armoury_code (sensitive) and club_region. The files armoury/keypad-code.txt and armoury/door-card.txt must be built from the environment values, with the keypad code file mode 0600.

mission.name: Acacia Ridge Passphrase
mission.description: The Acacia Ridge safari lodge's radio gets its admin passphrase from a local value that someone typed years ago, and every ranger who ever staffed the lodge knows it. The game reserve wants the passphrase generated by Terraform instead of living in the source.
mission.objective: Delete the hard-coded passphrase and generate it with a random_password resource named radio_admin (24+ characters with at least two lower-case, two upper-case and two numeric characters). radio/admin.conf must contain it as admin_passphrase=... with mode 0600, and the plan must stay clean on the next run.

mission.name: Orbital Spur Track Root
mission.description: The Orbital Spur hyperloop test track runs its own private certificate authority so the signal controller can prove who it is. The controller's certificate is generated, but the line operator's openssl check says it does not chain to the track root.
mission.objective: Make the controller certificate (pki/signals.pem, CN signals.orbitalspur.test) verify against the track root (pki/root-ca.pem) with openssl verify. The root must be a real CA that can sign certificates, and the controller certificate must stay an ordinary end-entity (not CA) certificate.

mission.name: Kestrel Junction Charger Certificate
mission.description: The Kestrel Junction EV charging hub's charger controller carries a self-signed certificate that was issued with a validity of just six hours and no renewal window. The hub operator wants it replaced with a certificate that lasts months and that Terraform starts renewing a week before it runs out.
mission.objective: Rotate the certificate in pki/charger.pem (a new serial) so it is valid for at least 60 days, and configure early_renewal_hours of at least 168 (and below the validity) on tls_self_signed_cert.charger. The plan must be clean afterwards and pki/charger.key must stay mode 0600.

mission.name: Fiddlestick Locker Combination
mission.description: The Fiddlestick & Sons circus rotates the rigging-locker combination by raising a ticket number, but the generated password changes on every single apply, and riggers keep getting locked out mid-show. The password resource was given a keepers map in an attempt to tie it to something.
mission.objective: Make the combination change only when var.rotation_ticket changes: stable across repeated plans and applies, new after raising the ticket (for example to RIG-101), and stable again afterwards.

mission.name: Marrowby Chimney Sweep Key
mission.description: A chimney sweep round's nightly job-sheet sync logs in over SFTP with a key pair generated by Terraform. The private half is written next to the public half with ordinary file settings, and the sync tool now refuses to start, complaining that the private key is readable by others.
mission.objective: Write the private key to keys/sweepround_ed25519 as a sensitive file with mode 0600 inside a keys/ directory of mode 0700, so ssh-keygen accepts it. The public key file and the public_key output must keep working.

mission.name: Ashgrove Deed Box
mission.description: A notary's digital deed register is sealed with a generated master passphrase, which Terraform also writes to a key file. Last week an intern ran terraform destroy in the wrong terminal and the team had to restore the passphrase from a printed backup.
mission.objective: Make Terraform refuse to destroy the master passphrase (random_password.box_master) and the key file (local_sensitive_file.deed_register): terraform plan -destroy must fail for both, normal plans must stay clean, and the existing passphrase must not change.

mission.name: Lindenhurst Gate Rules
mission.description: The retirement village committee tightened its gate rules in code last month, and terraform plan has reported no changes ever since. When a resident checked the actual rules file, the gate was still open to the whole internet. Someone silenced a noisy diff during a rushed release.
mission.objective: Find what keeps the tightened rules from being applied. After a successful apply, gate/access-rules.json must allow only 10.20.0.0/16 with mode 0640, and later edits to the rules in code must show up in plans again.

mission.name: Saint Odran Gateway Policy
mission.description: The Saint Odran scriptorium's archive gateway is supposed to accept only internal networks and modern TLS. The variable validation that enforces this was written in a hurry, and a reviewer has found inputs that sail straight through it.
mission.objective: Tighten the two validation rules so that allowed_cidrs must be non-empty, contain only valid networks, none shorter than a /8 (so never 0.0.0.0/0, ::/0 or 0.0.0.0/1), and min_tls_version is only 1.2 or 1.3. The default values and normal inputs such as IPv6 ULA ranges must keep working.

mission.name: Halloway Shelf Policy
mission.description: The Halloway pawnbroker's shop has a rule that every storage shelf holds its pledged items at least 30 days and is never public. A precondition on the shelf manifests was meant to enforce it, but a reviewer found shelves that break the rule happily applying.
mission.objective: Make the precondition on local_file.shelf_manifest enforce the policy (retention_days of at least 30 and public = false) so that violating shelves fail with a resource precondition error, and bring the shop's own default shelves into compliance without removing any of them.

mission.name: Ridgeway Gliding Key Audit
mission.description: The Ridgeway gliding club signs its flight logbook entries with a secret kept in a key file, and an audit step reads the file's real mode after Terraform has created it. The audit only checks that the file exists, and the key is currently created readable by everyone on the clubhouse server.
mission.objective: Make the postcondition on data.external.key_audit fail whenever the key file is not mode 600, and make the default key_mode produce a compliant 0600 file. An apply with a looser key_mode (0644, 0640, 0660) must fail with a postcondition error.

mission.name: Redline Kart Track Token
mission.description: A go-kart track publishes its booking calendar through a gateway with a local-exec provisioner. The gateway token is a sensitive variable, but an auditor opened terraform.tfstate and found the token sitting in it in plain text.
mission.objective: Keep calling bin/publish.sh with GATEWAY_TOKEN in its environment, but make sure the token never ends up in the state file: declare it as an ephemeral variable and stop storing it in the resource's input. The published_track output must keep working.

mission.name: Emberfall Ignore List
mission.description: The Emberfall ice sculpture festival's Terraform repo has a prod.tfvars with the ice supplier payment key in it and a short .gitignore that someone wrote from memory. Last week a teammate's git add . picked up a state backup, and nobody noticed that the one file meant to be committed, the provider lock file, is on the ignore list.
mission.objective: Fix .gitignore so that .terraform/ directories, every kind of state file (terraform.tfstate, .backup, workspace states, errored.tfstate), saved plan files (*.tfplan), secret variable files (*.tfvars and *.tfvars.json) and crash logs are ignored, while *.tf files, .terraform.lock.hcl and terraform.tfvars.example stay tracked. reports/ignore-audit.txt must keep matching the live rules.

mission.name: Night Taxi Dispatch Hand-off
mission.description: A night taxi rank generates a one-shot session token inside a small issuer module and leaves it in a dispatch box through a provisioner. The token comes from an ephemeral resource so it should never be stored, yet Terraform refuses to plan the root module.
mission.objective: Make the config apply so the token created by the issuer module's ephemeral random_password reaches handoff/session.token, while it appears nowhere in the state file. Keep the ephemeral resource in the module, and do not replace it with a regular random_password.

mission.name: Fossil Pit Wiring
mission.description: The Hollin Quarry dig site stamps every specimen tag through a provider configuration named after its pit. After a rushed edit, terraform validate complains about a provider configuration that was never declared, and one reference is written in the old quoted style.
mission.objective: Make random_id.north_tag use the north_pit configuration and random_id.south_tag use the south_pit configuration, both as bare references (no quotes). The configuration must apply, state must record each tag under its own alias, and dig/specimens.txt must list both tags.

mission.name: Back Wall Spare Reel
mission.description: The Quillfeather Fishing Tackle Shop moved reel serial numbering into a module. Inside it, the spare reel asks for a provider configuration called random.spare, but terraform validate says that configuration is missing, as if it had been removed.
mission.objective: Give the reel_stock module a proper declaration of the extra provider configuration it needs, and pass the root's random.back_wall configuration into it. The spare reel must be tracked in state under the back_wall alias, the primary reel on the default configuration, and terraform validate must be free of warnings.

mission.name: Billboard Never Goes Dark
mission.description: Roadside Billboard Co. writes its highway board with create_before_destroy so the sign is never blank. This week's advert changed and the apply 'succeeds', yet the sign file is gone afterwards and the next plan wants to create it again.
mission.objective: Keep create_before_destroy, replace the board with this week's advert (ON THE BOARD: Sunrise Cereal Summer Sale), and end up with a board file on disk, no leftover file for last week's advert, and a clean plan.

mission.name: Reflash On Release
mission.description: Controller GT-114 at the Bumper & Flip Ghost Train just got firmware 3.2. The operations team wanted the controller record rebuilt on every firmware release, yet the plan only shows a small in-place update for the firmware pack and leaves the controller alone.
mission.objective: Make a firmware change replace terraform_data.controller (new ID) while terraform_data.calibration and terraform_data.firmware_pack keep their IDs. Apply, and finish with a clean plan and an up-to-date service/gt-114.txt.

mission.name: Master Key Moves Backwards
mission.description: Hollis & Daughter Locksmiths renamed the safe's master key resource from master to master_key and added a moved block to keep it. Now terraform plan refuses to run at all and complains about a 'moved object' that 'still exists'.
mission.objective: Repair the moved block so it records the rename in the right direction. The key must keep its fingerprint under tls_private_key.master_key, the register file must not be rewritten, and the plan must be clean.

mission.name: Shaft A Becomes North
mission.description: The Kallmark salt mine inspects each shaft through a module call. The first call was renamed from shaft_a to north_shaft, and the plan now wants to throw away the north shaft's inspection tag and placard and issue new ones.
mission.objective: Keep the new module call name north_shaft and the south shaft untouched. Use a single moved block to move the whole module instance, so the north tag and placard keep their IDs, and finish with a clean plan.

mission.name: Trebuchet Ledger Goes Built-In
mission.description: The Hartley Heath Trebuchet Society is dropping the null provider and switched its launch ledger from null_resource to the built-in terraform_data. Terraform now rejects the config, and even after fixing that it would throw away the ledger ID that is already printed on every shot card.
mission.objective: Convert the ledger to terraform_data.launch_ledger using the argument the new type actually has and a moved block from null_resource.launch_ledger. The ID must stay the same, the shot card must not be rewritten, and the plan must be clean.

mission.name: Target Seven Stands Down
mission.description: Fletcher's Meadow Archery Range is closing target 7 permanently. The block was replaced by a removed block that was copied from last month's 'just stop managing it' migration, so the scorecard stays on disk and the retirement receipt never gets written.
mission.objective: Decommission target 7 properly: its scorecard targets/target-7.txt must be destroyed, the destroy-time provisioner must leave receipts/target-7.txt, target 7 must be gone from state, and targets 5 and 6 must keep their IDs.

mission.name: Key Number Rk9mPg
mission.description: The alpine club's Eagle's Nest hut register moved into its own module. The brass key tag says Rk9mPg, and that exact number has to be adopted into the module, but terraform plan complains that the import target does not exist in the configuration.
mission.objective: Adopt the existing key number Rk9mPg into module.hut.random_id.key with an import block in the root module. Afterwards the key hex must come from that adopted ID, the hut mascot must keep its name, and the plan must be clean.

mission.name: Four Shaping Tickets
mission.description: Saltwater Shapers surfboard workshop is retiring its old ticket software. Four paper job tickets are already pinned to blanks on the racks, but only the longboard job was written as an import. The plan shows the other three being created with brand-new numbers.
mission.objective: Adopt all four tickets (longboard 4021, shortboard 7316, fish 2288, gun 5907) with a single import block that loops over var.legacy_tickets. Nothing is created, the shaper keeps their codename, and shop/queue.txt lists the original numbers in alphabetical order.

mission.name: Numbered, Launched And Corked
mission.description: The Cooper's Ridge Message-in-a-Bottle Society keeps a paper register of a bottle number, a launch timestamp and a cork code, and wants them adopted into Terraform. All three import blocks use the register values, but each provider expects its own import ID format, so the plan fails or wants to replace what it imported.
mission.objective: Correct the three import IDs so bottle 212, launch time 2025-04-12T06:30:00Z and cork code Yd4Pxg are adopted exactly, nothing is destroyed or replaced, and society/certificate.txt shows the register values. Keep each import pointed at the same resource.

mission.name: Varnish Batch Guard
mission.description: The Lindqvist violin workshop guards each varnish batch with two postconditions: no more than 5 litres, at least 5 days of cure. The rules mention the batch record by its own name, and Terraform says a resource's configuration may not refer to itself.
mission.objective: Keep both rules as postconditions on terraform_data.varnish_batch, rewrite them so they are legal, and apply so labels/vx-2210.txt reads 'VX-2210: 4 L, cure 6 days'.

mission.name: Squash Ladder Guards
mission.description: The Baseline Squash Club reads its monthly court ladder from a CSV export. The guard that should stop a bad export was written as a single precondition that reads the data source's own content, and Terraform refuses to load the configuration.
mission.objective: Guard data.local_file.ladder properly: a precondition that rejects a missing file or a name that does not end in .csv before the read, and a postcondition that rejects content whose header is not rank,player,rating. The default ladder must still plan and apply and the champion output must be 'Ingrid Halvorsen'.

mission.name: Two Loops One Tooling Kit
mission.description: Oak & Awl packs a tooling kit zip per workshop with a dynamic block fed by two nested loops. Terraform plan fails because the content block refers to a name that no longer exists, and once that is fixed the zip entries are named 0/belt.txt instead of north/belt.txt.
mission.objective: Make the kit hold exactly east/satchel.txt, north/belt.txt and north/wallet.txt, each containing 'stitch sheet for <piece>'. Keep the dynamic source block and the loop over var.workshops.

mission.name: Axe Bar Tfvars Writer
mission.description: The Blue Note axe-throwing bar generates the settings file for its booking stack from a Terraform object, and reads last month's file back to compute how many seats were added. The config uses Terraform's built-in provider functions, but Terraform says they do not exist.
mission.objective: Make the encode_tfvars and decode_tfvars calls work as they are written: stack/night.tfvars must be the encode_tfvars rendering of the venue object and the output seat_growth must be 8.

mission.name: Piano Ticket Closing Line
mission.description: Wren & Hammer piano tuning logs 'opened' and 'closed' for every tuning ticket using provisioners on a terraform_data record. The closing line is written when the ticket is destroyed, but Terraform refuses the configuration because of what that provisioner refers to.
mission.objective: Keep both provisioners and make the destroy-time one legal by reading the ticket through self. Afterwards visits/diary.log must show 'opened PT-2041 (Steinbeck upright piano)', and replacing the ticket must append 'closed PT-2041'.

mission.name: Key That Never Lands
mission.description: ZipWheel E-Scooter Rental wants scooter 07's private key to exist only during the run. The key is an ephemeral resource, but handing it to the certificate request makes Terraform refuse with 'Invalid use of ephemeral value'.
mission.objective: Keep the ephemeral tls_private_key and sign the request with it through the argument that is allowed to take ephemeral values. The CSR must be saved to pki/scooter-07.csr, no private key may appear in the state, and the plan must be clean afterwards.

mission.name: Turbidity Sensor Warning
mission.description: Millbrook Water Treatment Plant writes a shift report for clarifier 4 and wants to hear about a degraded turbidity sensor without losing the report. At the moment a precondition blocks the whole apply whenever the sensor file does not say ok.
mission.objective: Turn the sensor rule into a non-blocking check with its own scoped data source. The shift report must be written, terraform plan must show a 'Check block assertion failed' warning while clarifier/status.txt says degraded, and no resource changes may be pending.

mission.name: Stools For Every Student
mission.description: The Cocktail Masterclass Bar must never plan more students than stools, and a class must end after it starts. The seating rule only exists as a late precondition inside a resource, and the hours are not checked at all, so nonsense combinations get a long way into the plan.
mission.objective: Enforce both rules where the inputs are declared: with variable validation blocks that compare variables with each other. terraform plan must reject impossible combinations with 'Invalid value for variable', accept a full house and any other consistent values, and the default plan must still produce class/plan.txt.

mission.name: Bounce Hollow Big Bang
mission.description: Bounce Hollow trampoline park merged a large refactor into one commit: court wristbands and cards moved from count to for_each, the kangaroo mascot left the configuration, and the scoreboard high score must now be managed. Terraform sees none of that intent and plans to destroy and recreate almost everything.
mission.objective: Describe all three changes in code (moved blocks, a removed block with destroy = false, an import block) so that the plan has no destroys or replacements: the three court wristbands and cards keep their IDs under name keys, the mascot leaves state while its costume stays valid, high score 7421 is adopted, and the plan ends clean.

mission.name: Sled Check Trace
mission.description: Frostline Snowmobile Tours writes its sled check sheets with Terraform. Last night's apply died halfway through, the on-call engineer pasted a vague error into the channel, and the morning departure briefing is now waiting. Support also wants the exact plugin version from the trace for their ticket.
mission.objective: Capture a trace with TF_LOG and TF_LOG_PATH, find which resource failed and during which provider call, then fix the configuration so apply succeeds and the plan stays clean. Write answers/trace.txt with exactly three lines: failed_resource=<resource address>, failed_rpc=<PlanResourceChange or ApplyResourceChange> and provider_version=<version of the local provider that ran>.

mission.name: Archive Door Schema
mission.description: The Garnet & Gold Couture House issues a new door code and schedules its next inventory audit from a small Terraform config. Someone wrote the arguments from memory and now every resource block is rejected with "Unsupported argument" - and the docs site is down for maintenance.
mission.objective: Use the provider schemas that Terraform already has on disk (terraform providers schema -json) to find the real argument names, then make apply succeed: an 18 character code without special characters in archive/door-code.txt with file mode 0600, and an audit_due output exactly 30 days after 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z.

mission.name: Antenna Time Console
mission.description: The Kestrel ground station books antenna time from a CSV of satellite passes embedded in its Terraform config. The planning sheet came out with the wrong satellites on it, and after a quick edit the per-family totals refuse to evaluate at all. Nobody wants to apply again just to find out what an expression returns.
mission.objective: Use terraform console to evaluate the pieces of the locals and repair the expressions. longest_windows must be ["HERON-3","OSPREY-5","HERON-4"] (usable passes only, longest first), total_usable_minutes must be 239 and per_family_minutes must map each family to a list of numeric minutes, e.g. HERON = [120, 15].

mission.name: Sprayer Flash Recovery
mission.description: Critter Clear Pest Control flashes new firmware onto the sprayer controller in each van from a local-exec provisioner. Yesterday's rollout to van-07 failed halfway, and Terraform has marked the resource as tainted. The next apply wants to replace it - but the same failure is waiting.
mission.objective: Find out why the flash script failed (read its output), repair the configuration, and let Terraform replace the tainted terraform_data.sprayer_firmware so that flashed/van-07.stamp exists. The resource must be recreated by a successful provisioner run: untainting it or hiding the failure does not count.

mission.name: Patrol Roster Cycle
mission.description: The Elmwood Neighbourhood Watch publishes a roster and a schedule for its Tuesday patrol from Terraform. The roster quotes the schedule's checksum so walkers can tell they have matching sheets, and the schedule points walkers to the roster file. After the last edit, plan stops with an "Error: Cycle".
mission.objective: Break the dependency cycle without deleting either file and without depends_on: patrol/roster.txt must contain the line "schedule checksum: " followed by the real SHA-256 of patrol/schedule.txt (computed by Terraform, not typed), and patrol/schedule.txt must still mention the roster file path patrol/roster.txt.

mission.name: Blind Tasting Count
mission.description: The Golden Crunch crisp factory shuffles five flavours and prints one blind-tasting card for each flavour picked for the panel. Planning stops with "Invalid count argument ... depends on resource attributes that cannot be determined until apply", even though the panel size is just a variable.
mission.objective: Make the number of cards known at plan time while still printing a card per flavour on the shuffled panel: with the default panel_size of 3, apply must create cards/card-1.txt to card-3.txt with three different flavours from the shuffle, and planning with -var panel_size=4 must work and add exactly one more card.

mission.name: Album Index Churn
mission.description: The Lumen Cartophilic Society publishes its trading-card album index file from Terraform. Every plan - even straight after an apply, with nobody touching anything - wants to rewrite it, and the CI job that expects "No changes" has been red for a week.
mission.objective: Find out why plans never settle and fix every source of the churn: after one apply, repeated plans must show no changes. album/index.md must keep its "Generated:" line as an RFC 3339 timestamp stamped once at creation, and list the cards alphabetically. Do not paper over it with ignore_changes.

mission.name: Dive Log Signer
mission.description: Blue Reef Dive School already runs a boat logbook from Terraform. This morning a colleague pulled a branch that starts signing the logs with a TLS key, and now every Terraform command refuses to work in the existing checkout.
mission.objective: Read the error to find out which provider is missing, record its full source address in answers/missing.txt as the single line missing_provider=<source address>, then bring the working directory up to date from the command line and apply, so the signing key and divelog/signature.txt exist while the existing boat name stays unchanged.

mission.name: Willow Wren Version Clash
mission.description: Willow Wren Houseboat Rental generates its weekend booking sheet through two small local modules. Since the galley module was copied in from an older repository, terraform init fails with "no available releases match the given constraints" and nobody can plan.
mission.objective: Work out which constraints cannot be satisfied together and fix the module that is too strict, so that a single version of the random provider (3.6 or newer, as the root module requires) serves the whole configuration. Both modules and the booking sheet in boat/booking.txt must keep working.

mission.name: Community Board Tug of War
mission.description: Two volunteers at the Riverside Community Centre each added a Terraform resource that writes the main-hall noticeboard. Every plan now wants to rewrite the file, every apply "fixes" one half and breaks the other, and the board shows only the standing text or only the events list depending on who ran Terraform last.
mission.objective: Make exactly one resource own board/notices.md so that it holds both the standing text and the events list (intro first, a blank line, then "## Events" and the dated bullets) and the plan stays clean on every run. Keep the local values that define the texts.

mission.name: Telephone Box Service Duplicate
mission.description: Rewind Telephone Box Restorations registers each telephone box's service code in Terraform. A technician wanted to "re-adopt" the telephone box and imported its code under a second, temporary resource name, then deleted the temporary block from the code. Now plan wants to destroy something that is not in the configuration - and that something is the same telephone box the real resource manages.
mission.objective: Find out which state entry duplicates random_integer.service_code and remove only the duplicate from state, without destroying anything. The service code must stay unchanged, the code must keep the single resource random_integer.service_code, and the plan must be clean.

mission.name: Silent Binding Failure
mission.description: Pressed & Proper Bookbindery starts each binding run from a local-exec provisioner. The pipeline has been green all week, yet the bindery log for batch 114 does not exist and the customers' books are still unbound. Someone added a setting to keep the pipeline green when the script complains.
mission.objective: Remove the setting that hides the failure, repair the real cause so the script succeeds, and make Terraform run the provisioner again on the existing resource (it is already in state and counted as successfully created). bindery/batch-114.log must contain batch=batch-114 press=20C status=bound, written by the provisioner.

mission.name: Studio Notes Not Found
mission.description: The Harbour Lane recording studio writes the engineer's session notes with one resource and quotes them on the producer's track sheet in another. On a fresh checkout terraform plan stops with "no file exists at studio/notes.txt", although the very next resource is supposed to create that file.
mission.objective: Make a fresh workspace plan and apply successfully without creating studio/notes.txt by hand: the track sheet must still quote the notes, studio/track-sheet.txt must begin with "Session notes (3 takes):", and the take_count output must be 3. Terraform, not you, must be the thing that writes the notes file.

mission.name: Lost Property Tags
mission.description: Central Station's lost property office prints a tag for every item in the cage from a map of objects. Some items have been claimed and carry a holder and an optional phone number; others have no claim at all. Plan dies with "Attempt to get attribute from null value" as soon as an unclaimed item is in the list.
mission.objective: Make the tags work for claimed and unclaimed items alike, computed from the data. cage/tags.txt must have one line per item in the form name: description | holder=HOLDER | phone=PHONE, with the holder upper-cased, "UNCLAIMED" when nobody has claimed it and "n/a" when there is no phone number. The validator also plans with other items, so do not hard-code the defaults.

mission.name: Spillway Gate Certificates
mission.description: The Ironvale Dam Authority's spillway gate certificates were written years ago for the tls provider 3.x. The constraint now says "~> 4.0" and every plan fails with "Invalid Configuration for Read-Only Attribute" on arguments that used to be required.
mission.objective: Migrate the configuration to the tls 4.x schema without downgrading the provider: spillway/spillway-4.crt and spillway/spillway-4.csr must be created for spillway-4.ironvale-dam.example (organization Ironvale Dam Authority), the self-signed certificate must last 720 hours, and the plan must be clean afterwards.

mission.name: Comic Con Legacy Syntax
mission.description: The Nova City Comic Con organisers inherited a Terraform repository written for version 0.11 in 2017. It prints the programme and price board, but today's Terraform rejects it: quoted type names, list() and map() calls, and a wall of deprecation warnings (interpolation-only expressions, quoted references in depends_on).
mission.objective: Modernise the syntax without changing what the config produces: con/programme.txt must read "Nova City Comic Con", "Stalls: posters, cards, figures" and "Extras: cosplay, meet and greet"; con/prices.txt must list cards, figures, posters and then the two extras sorted by name; outputs stall_count = 3 and extras = ["cosplay","meet and greet"]. terraform validate must finish with zero errors and zero warnings.

mission.name: Olive Oil Bottling Graph
mission.description: The Sunridge Olive Oil Mill's bottling paperwork is generated from seven linked resources, and the dispatch step sometimes fails on a fresh checkout with "bottling/manifest.txt is missing" - and works when you just run the apply again. The mill manager also asks two questions about the setup: which resource has the most others hanging off it, and how long the longest chain of "must exist before" is.
mission.objective: Use terraform graph to read the dependency edges. Write answers/graph.txt with two lines, hub=<address of the managed resource with the most direct dependents> and longest_chain=<number of managed resources on the longest dependency chain, after your fix>, and then fix the configuration so dispatch can only start after the manifest exists. A fresh apply must succeed every time.

mission.name: Diamond Mine Crash Log
mission.description: The Brightstone diamond mine's overnight CI job died with a plugin crash instead of a normal error, and the only thing it left behind is crash.log in the workspace. The morning shaft inspection report has not been produced and the safety officer wants to know exactly what crashed.
mission.objective: Read crash.log, find the resource that crashed and the offending key, and write answers/crash.txt with exactly two lines: crashed_resource=<resource address> and offending_key=<key name>. Then change the configuration so that this path no longer gets the shape that crashed it: reports/shaft-b.txt must say "Shaft B inspected by R. Voss: deepest reading 311 m", computed from the probe's readings, with a clean plan afterwards.

mission.name: Sugar-Glass Melt Order
mission.description: The Cobbleton Sugar-Glass Stage-Prop Workshop writes a label slip from the syrup ledger every time the stove config is applied. Since the team upgraded to a faster CI runner the apply fails most mornings with "No such file or directory", yet it "worked on my laptop" back when everything ran one step at a time. Somebody already pasted -parallelism=1 into the deploy script as a workaround.
mission.objective: Make a normal parallel apply succeed every time. The label slip step must read the syrup ledger only after the ledger exists, and workshop/label-slip.txt must contain the ledger text. No -parallelism flag anywhere (script or config), and no sleep or polling loop in the command.

mission.name: Stockroom Cull
mission.description: The Madcap Fancy Dress Hire stockroom team tried to retire one record with "terraform destroy -target=local_file.costume_register". Terraform warned about the target, then quietly took the fitting roster and the dry-cleaning notice down as well, because both are built on top of the register. Halloween weekend starts on Friday.
mission.objective: Bring everything back without a -target flag: all four resources in state, the rack seal unchanged, the register, roster and notices.log in place, and a clean plan. The dry-cleaning notice must have fired exactly once more than the original run (notices.log has 2 lines).

mission.name: Chiller Audit Shortcut
mission.description: Greenfield Market keeps one setpoint file per chilled-aisle unit. Plans took too long, so somebody gave ops/plan.sh a -refresh=false flag, and both its "quick" mode (used while editing code) and its "audit" mode (used by the nightly drift check) now share it. Last night a technician deleted the file for chiller yoghurt-b and the audit reported all clear.
mission.objective: Keep "ops/plan.sh quick" fast (it must still skip the refresh and report no changes while the drift is unfixed), but make "ops/plan.sh audit" refresh real infrastructure so that it exits 2 and names yoghurt-b. Any other mode must still exit non-zero.

mission.name: Geyser Feed Reconcile
mission.description: Geyser 07 in the Whistling Basin Geyser Park reports into feeds/geyser-07.json, and the dashboard reads the eruption height straight from Terraform's outputs. The feed has moved on since the last apply, so the dashboard is stale. Meanwhile a colleague has left an unreviewed edit to the park banner in variables.tf, which a normal apply would push live.
mission.objective: Make Terraform's recorded output latest_height_m match the current feed, without applying the banner edit: banner.txt must keep its old text, the variables.tf edit must stay in place, and "terraform plan -refresh-only" must report nothing left to accept.

mission.name: Scrapyard Identity Split
mission.description: The Rustfield scrapyard has one Terraform state for everything: the yard identity (a random name and the gate count, both painted on trucks and printed on waste-licence forms) and the crane roster that the shift planners change daily. Every roster tweak makes the platform team wait on a plan that also refreshes the yard identity. Time to partition: the identity moves to its own configuration under core/, and the roster configuration reads it from there.
mission.objective: Create core/ as its own root module that owns random_pet.yard_name and random_integer.gate_count (with outputs yard_name and gate_count), move those two objects into core/terraform.tfstate without changing their values, and make the root configuration read them through a terraform_remote_state data source. Both root and core must plan clean.

mission.name: Crayon Factory Split
mission.description: Wax & Wonder makes crayons. One module, modules/workshop, pours the wax batch, cuts the colour spec and prints the label, and every new product line wants only part of it: the wholesale line has no labels, the refill line has no colour. Batch IDs are already printed on boxes in the warehouse, so nothing may be destroyed along the way.
mission.objective: Replace modules/workshop with three composable modules: modules/pour (random_id.batch and local_file.pour_sheet), modules/colour (local_file.colour_spec) and modules/label (local_file.label, fed by the outputs of the other two). The root calls module.pour, module.colour and module.label, the existing objects end up at the new addresses with the same batch ID, and the plan is clean.

mission.name: Stadium Seat Tags
mission.description: Fairmount Park stadium prints a tag file for every one of its 300 seats, and the config that makes them is 300 hand-pasted resource blocks. Adding a new block of seats means pasting ten more and hoping nobody mistypes a row number; last season two seats shipped with identical tags. The groundskeepers also need the same files to stay in place: re-creating a tag reprints it.
mission.objective: Replace the 300 resource blocks with exactly one data-driven local_file resource using for_each (6 blocks A-F, rows 1-5, seats 01-10; keys like "a-1-01"). The 300 existing tag files must be moved to the new addresses (local_file.seat["a-1-01"], ...) with no destroy or replace, and the plan must end clean.

mission.name: Tree Order Approval Plan
mission.description: Ludlow Heritage Tree Preservation Office's change process says the officer who applies the register must apply exactly the plan the head arborist signed off, not whatever a fresh plan looks like at apply time. The head arborist approved plan.tfplan this morning, but before the officer could use it another officer applied one of the new orders by hand. Now "terraform apply plan.tfplan" refuses to run.
mission.objective: Get all five orders (register/t-3011 ... t-3015) onto disk by applying a freshly saved plan file: plan.tfplan must be a new, valid saved plan that still contained the creations you applied, it must differ from the stale one the level started with, and the plan must be clean afterwards.

mission.name: Whisky Bond Gate
mission.description: Glenmorrow Distillery runs a whisky bonded warehouse whose manifests are managed in Terraform. Before any plan may be applied, the pipeline pipes "terraform show -json" into policy/check.sh and blocks on a non-zero exit. The script was written in a hurry: last week a replacement of a manifest file sailed through, a world-readable manifest was approved, and a plan file that could not even be read was reported as compliant.
mission.objective: Fix policy/check.sh so it follows policy/RULES.txt exactly: exit 0 for a compliant plan, 1 when a rule is broken (printing one VIOLATION line per problem), 2 when the plan file is missing or not JSON. It is tested against many prepared plans plus the real plan of this workspace.

mission.name: Render Farm Plugin Shelf
mission.description: Kiln Street Studios runs forty throwaway CI agents, and each one downloads the same provider plugins on every "terraform init". The platform engineer added a CLI config file, ci/terraform.rc, to share a plugin cache, but the agents' init logs still say "Installing ..." for every run and nothing ever appears in the cache folder.
mission.objective: Fix ci/terraform.rc and ci/agent-setup.sh so a CI agent gets a working shared plugin cache: plugin_cache_dir must be an existing directory under $HOME (a literal ~ is not expanded), agent-setup.sh must create exactly that directory, checkpoint phone-home must be disabled, and two separate working directories initialised with this config must both link their providers from the same cache.

mission.name: Shard Tray Index Costs
mission.description: Brightbox Kaleidoscope Workshop builds kaleidoscopes from a catalogue of glass shards. Their Terraform plan, which feeds six index files and two outputs from one catalogue, takes longer every time the catalogue grows. A profiler trace shows the same JSON being read, parsed and hashed over and over: jsondecode(file(...)) appears in twelve places and the checksum is recomputed three times.
mission.objective: Compute the decoded catalogue and the checksum once, in locals, and have everything else read them. The config may contain jsondecode(...) exactly once and sha256(...) exactly once, must use a locals block, and every generated file and output must come out byte-identical, so the plan stays clean.

mission.name: Traffic Light Monorepo
mission.description: Mapleton Crossroads' traffic-light team keeps three subsystems (junction controller, bus priority, crossing countdown) in one root module and one state file, so a bus-priority tweak locks the junction-controller plan and one failed apply blocks everybody. They already share a module library, modules/plan_sheet. Each subsystem should be its own root module with its own state, still built from the shared library.
mission.objective: Create components/junction-controller, components/bus-priority and components/crossing-countdown. Each is a standalone root module (its own terraform.tf and local state) calling ../../modules/plan_sheet and writing out/<component>.txt with the same lines as today. The repository root must no longer declare any module or resource. The validator initialises and applies every component separately.

mission.name: Mudflat Stage Contract
mission.description: At the Mudflat Music Festival the stage team owns modules/stage, and two other teams build on its outputs: lighting reads the power budget, rigging reads "power_kw". During a tidy-up the stage team renamed power_kw to power_budget_kw and the rigging pipeline broke on a Friday night. Both teams now want a written contract: a stable output with a version, and a transition period for old names.
mission.objective: In modules/stage, publish an output stage_contract (an object with exactly version, stage_id and power_budget_kw, where version comes from var.contract_version) and keep the old power_kw output alive with a deprecated message, so rigging.tf (which must stay untouched) works again. In lighting.tf, make the consumer refuse a contract whose major version is not 2 with a precondition.

mission.name: Pit Garage Lock File
mission.description: The Karakul Solar Car Challenge Team's laptops are a mix: two Apple-silicon Macs, a Linux build box, and a Windows field PC. Whoever generated .terraform.lock.hcl was on an Intel Mac, so it only records that platform's checksum, and every other machine stops at "terraform init" with a checksum mismatch error. The pit garage has no internet; the team vendors provider zips in vendor/provider-mirror for all the platforms it uses.
mission.objective: Make .terraform.lock.hcl cover linux_amd64, darwin_arm64 and windows_amd64 in addition to the platform it already has, using terraform providers lock against the vendored mirror (offline, no hand-edited hashes). The mirror files and the pinned null 3.3.2 must stay as they are, and init must still work.

mission.name: Lens Lab Gatekeeper
mission.description: Quillfeather Optics grinds prescription lenses and manages the order sheets in Terraform. Their merge-request job is ci/pipeline.sh, but it was written as a list of commands: it reformats files instead of checking them, waits for keyboard input that never comes, plans without saving anything, keeps going after failures and always ends with "pipeline done" and exit 0.
mission.objective: Rewrite ci/pipeline.sh as a real gate that runs, in this order, terraform fmt -check -recursive, terraform init -input=false, terraform validate and terraform plan -input=false -out=<planfile>; stops at the first failing step with a non-zero exit; never rewrites files or applies; leaves a valid saved plan after a good run; and works no matter which directory it is started from.

mission.name: Meridian Detector Blackout
mission.description: 03:12 — the Meridian Particle Collider trigger system pages everyone: Terraform will not even list the ring's resources. A disk-full event cut terraform.tfstate off mid-write. There is a terraform.tfstate.backup next to it, but it is one apply old: the west station and the north station's retune were applied after it was taken. The trigger serials are burned into trigger-board firmware and cannot change before the 06:00 beam fill.
mission.objective: Make Terraform read a healthy state again and bring all four stations (north, south, east, west) under management with their ORIGINAL trigger serials. The final plan must be clean with nothing destroyed or replaced, and calibration/station-north.cfg must show the 1420.4 kHz retune.

mission.name: Harrow Tempering Hall Drift
mission.description: Harrow Chocolate Tempering Hall starts a new dark-chocolate campaign at dawn and the pre-run audit finds the control files disagree with Terraform in five different ways. A tech mistyped kettle A's chill time, kettle B's file vanished in a PLC swap, the foreman hot-fixed the temper recipe with the quality lab's blessing (ticket INC-4471), mold C was scrapped and its file removed, and somebody tainted the campaign cocoa lot although the wrappers have already shipped.
mission.objective: Reconcile all five objects in the right direction. Kettle A gets the code's chill time back, kettle B's file is restored, the approved 122 F melt temperature becomes the new value in the code, mold C is retired from management for good, and the cocoa lot keeps its original ID. End with a clean plan and no pending destroy.

mission.name: Indigo Row Sorter Bump
mission.description: Indigo Row Recycling Plant authenticates its sorting-line optical sorters with a private CA that Terraform manages. Someone raised the tls provider constraint to ~> 4.0 and merged; now the pipeline is red on init, and an earlier attempt to "just make it validate" left the next plan threatening to replace key material. The sorters pin both the CA key and the sorter key; the first sort shift starts in the morning.
mission.objective: Upgrade the working directory to the 4.x tls provider (lock file included), repair the configuration for the arguments that no longer exist, and apply. Both private keys must keep their original IDs, the plan must end clean, and pki/sorter.pem must verify against pki/ca.pem.

mission.name: Cedarbank Kiln Pipeline
mission.description: The Cedarbank Sawmill's drying pipeline died halfway through tonight's run. The ash lot's handshake with the kiln controller was rejected, the CI runner was killed before it wrote its state, and on-call tainted one healthy run in the confusion. Pallet tags are already printed and wrapped on the wood in the yard, and the yard office needs tickets for all three lots before the 07:00 shift.
mission.objective: Finish the pipeline for the oak, pine and ash lots. Every pallet tag keeps its printed number, the oak and pine kiln runs keep their IDs, the ash run is redone successfully on the right kiln, all three tickets are tracked in state, and the plan ends clean.

mission.name: Calder Reach Annex Teardown
mission.description: Change CHG-2291 retires the north annex berths at Calder Reach Shipyard. The change is merged (annex_enabled = false) but every plan stops cold: an audit added prevent_destroy to the annex's berth tag, the very thing being retired. Meanwhile the one object that must never be destroyed, the serial on the yard's operating charter filed with the harbour authority, has no protection at all, and the harbour master wants the annex gone today.
mission.objective: Complete the decommission so the annex objects are destroyed and removed from state. The charter serial must keep its ID, carry the only prevent_destroy guard in the configuration, and the yard manifest must no longer reference the annex. Finish with a clean plan.

mission.name: Tern Field Baggage Cascade
mission.description: The capacity-aware sortation release rewrote all three baggage-hall modules at once and the morning departure bank is minutes away. CI shows one red error in the belts module and nothing else, but the sorter and dispatch modules sit behind it and nobody has seen their plans yet. Belt controllers have their serial numbers engraved, so those cannot change.
mission.objective: Repair the module chain end to end: belts, then sorters, then dispatch. All four belt serials and both sorter names keep their existing values, total_capacity must evaluate to 130 and busiest_sorter to transfer by computation, and the plan must finish clean.

mission.name: Pellham Docket Lineage Clash
mission.description: A botched cleanup session erased the filing seal and courtroom c2's call-sign from the live state at Pellham Municipal Court. A clerk has a full copy on a laptop, but terraform state push refuses it, and the copy is also stale: courtroom c3's call-sign was legitimately re-rolled after it was taken (CHG-0710), and it still lists a decommissioned archive index. Printed binders carry the real values; the court sits at 09:00.
mission.objective: Restore the missing docket seal and the c2 call-sign from recovery/docket-snapshot.tfstate without changing the live state's lineage and with a serial higher than the incident state's. c3 must keep its newer call-sign, the archive index must not return, and the plan must be clean with nothing destroyed.

mission.name: Halden Field B Teardown
mission.description: Sunday night's Field B teardown at Halden Marquee Hire died partway: the runner was killed after marquee m1 was handed back, mid-way through m2. The landowner wants the field empty and the rigs returned by morning, but now nothing moves. The site plan fails to render with Field B switched off, the rigging handover refuses to run, and a tags file for marquee m3 is lying around with no state behind it. The client register must survive for next season's contracts.
mission.objective: Finish the teardown: every Field B object gone from state, all three rigs returned through the real handover (crates/unrig.log shows m1, m2 and m3), no leftover tags files, no stale lock, and the client register keeping its serial. End with a clean plan.

mission.name: Skerrow Roster Module v2
mission.description: The station-roster module vendored at Skerrow Point Lifeboat Station was bumped to v2.0 and the pipeline blocks the release. The v2 changelog lists renamed inputs and outputs, and quietly renamed two resources as well; a first draft of the plan wants to replace ten objects, which would repaint every helmet call-sign in the crew. A new default shift length of 8 hours is also due to take effect only after the crew welfare policy is signed next month.
mission.objective: Adopt v2 of the module in place: all five call-signs keep their values at the new v2 addresses, the duty cards still say shift 12h, nothing is destroyed or replaced, and the final plan is clean. The module's own renames should be handled so every consumer benefits.

mission.name: Karst Peak Id Rename
mission.description: A naming cleanup at Karst Peak Mountain Rescue renamed the station's callsign variable to an id at every layer of the dispatch radio plan, but three different people merged three different layers and nobody ran an end-to-end plan. The pipeline is red with an error that moves one layer deeper every time it is "fixed". Field radios are programmed with the current beacon serial and repeater channel, and the weekend search window opens in an hour.
mission.objective: Make the renamed variables line up from the root through region to post and supply the station identity MR-ALPINE-7 through the new names. The beacon serial and the repeater channel must keep their values, nothing may be destroyed or replaced, and the final plan must be clean.

mission.name: Nordhavn Orchid Reindex
mission.description: INCIDENT 0617 - Nordhavn Cold-Chain Orchid Auction House. A Friday refactor swapped every count-indexed resource for for_each and renamed two singletons, and Monday's pipeline plan wants to destroy and recreate 20 objects: six cart serials, seven lot-block numbers, five dock doors, the house licence and the opening timestamp. The lot slot numbers are printed on the auctioneer tablets and the licence is registered with the plant-health inspectorate.
mission.objective: Keep the refactored code (for_each, names random_id.cart, random_integer.lot, terraform_data.dock, random_uuid.house_licence, time_static.opening) and describe all 20 address changes with moved blocks, mapping each old index to the right new key. Every object must keep its original value, nothing may be destroyed and the plan must end clean.

mission.name: Harwick Stage Post Mixup
mission.description: INCIDENT 2209 - Harwick Rally Stage Marshals. During a night debugging session an engineer left the "staging" workspace selected and applied the hotfix branch. Four production stage marshal posts (forest-hairpin, quarry-jump, river-ford, summit-finish) now exist in the staging state, the prod workspace has never heard of them, and race control is loading post cards whose keys must not change.
mission.objective: Make the prod workspace the owner of the four post keys and cards with their original IDs, leave staging holding only its own region seed, and stop the config from pinning the environment so both workspaces plan cleanly with no destroys. Do not recreate any post key.

mission.name: Alderwater Cabinet Census
mission.description: INCIDENT 3342 - Alderwater defibrillator cabinet network. The city marathon is 36 hours away and the volunteer coordinator wants every defibrillator cabinet under Terraform before inspection rotas are generated from it. The cabinets already exist: their serial numbers are in the asset-database export register/cabinets.json, along with two retired sites that must stay out. The first attempt at adoption plans to mint 17 brand-new serials, which would invalidate every cabinet door label in the street.
mission.objective: Adopt the 15 active cabinets into random_id.cabinet[site] with import blocks driven by for_each over the register, so each one keeps the serial printed on its door label. Retired sites must not be managed, no serial may be typed into the code, the network key keeps its ID, and the plan must end clean with out/cabinet-roster.txt listing every active cabinet.

mission.name: Halcyon Float Stack Breakup
mission.description: INCIDENT 4108 - Halcyon Mardi Gras Float Warehouse. The one-state float warehouse stack has become so big that every krewe sign-up tweak locks the lighting team out of their deploys, and last night two plans collided. Change board CAB-4471 approved splitting it into warehouse, krewes and lighting stacks. The three new configs are scaffolded; the live objects are still all in monolith/. The rider capacity and bead series are already stamped on the float permits, so nothing may be re-issued.
mission.objective: Move every object out of the monolith state into the right new stack (warehouse/, krewes/, lighting/) without destroying or re-creating any of them: the former random_id.rig_key lives on as random_id.light_key. Lighting needs the gold bead series exported by krewes. Leave monolith/ empty of objects and resource code, and finish with clean plans in all three stacks.

mission.name: Hollowbrook Saffron Consolidation
mission.description: INCIDENT 5017 - Hollowbrook Saffron Growers' Co-op. The fields, drying and packing teams each run a private stack, and all three call their resources random_id.batch, random_integer.quota and local_file.ledger. The harvest deadline needs the field-to-jar chain in a single plan, so someone wrote a merged stack with one module per team. It has never been planned against real state, the packing team keeps its state in a workspace nobody remembers, and each team's quota and batch numbers are already on paperwork.
mission.objective: Merge the three team states into stacks/all-in-one so that module.fields, module.drying and module.packing each own their batch id, quota and ledger with the original values. The old team states must end up empty and their resource code retired. The merged stack must plan clean without destroying or replacing anything.

mission.name: Brannock Quota Blackout
mission.description: INCIDENT 6230 - Brannock Quay fish market. Tonight's landing-permit pipeline dies at plan time with "External Program Execution Failed" and one unhelpful stderr line. The security team rotated credentials last week; the previous night's run was cut off mid-stamp and left the trawler Marguerite's permit half issued. The vessel key is already printed on the trawler's paperwork.
mission.objective: Restore the pipeline using the information in logs/quota-lookup.log and the rotation hand-off: supply the correct production credential the way the rotation ticket demands (never in Terraform code, file mode 600), correct whatever else the log reveals, and make sure the interrupted permit stamp is genuinely redone. The vessel key must keep its ID, the tooling in bin/ must not be edited and the plan must end clean.

mission.name: Fenwick Lantern Overwrite
mission.description: INCIDENT 7184 - Fenwick Lantern Parade Volunteers. The volunteer build rota runs from a state file on the shared ops VM, and another team, restoring "last night's backup" for their own project, pushed a stale copy over it. Terraform now wants to create steward Cleo's badge, the owl bench slot and a fresh repair rack for the storm-damaged heron lantern, all of which already exist on paper and in the workshop. The recovery folder holds every copy anyone could find, and CI run 217's apply log, whose state upload failed.
mission.objective: Recover the correct state: use the freshest valid copy of this project's own state (same lineage, not just the highest serial), adopt the repair rack assigned by CI run 217 under its original number, and finish with a clean plan. Every badge, bench slot, the rota epoch and the rota file must keep its original ID, and nothing may be destroyed or re-issued.

mission.name: Kestrel Valley Truffle Hand Edit
mission.description: INCIDENT 8802 - Kestrel Valley Truffle-Hunting Estate. A teammate's migration script, run with a pre-release random provider build, rewrote terraform.tfstate before the build was withdrawn. Every Terraform command now refuses to read the state at all. The four hound tags and two grove harvest quotas are the ones certified by the truffle-licence inspector and stamped on the collars; re-rolling them means a new inspection before tomorrow's first dawn hunt.
mission.objective: Repair terraform.tfstate by hand, carefully: make Terraform able to read it again, put every hound tag and grove harvest quota back under its name with its certified value (out/inspection-log.txt is the evidence), keep the lineage and increase the serial. No destroy, no configuration change and a clean plan at the end.

mission.name: Aurelia Film Base Reset
mission.description: INCIDENT 9001 - Aurelia Midnight-Sun Film Shoot Base. The base laptop's disk filled during an apply and terraform.tfstate is cut off mid-file. The previous state backup is one apply old and misses the fuel tank registered last night. Meanwhile a colleague tainted the radio key and the dailies "to be safe", someone hand-edited the radio sheet, and a module refactor merged earlier left the configuration unable to plan at all. The generator serial, fuel figure and radio key are stamped on equipment.
mission.objective: Bring the base back: restore a readable state of the same lineage, repair the configuration errors that stop planning, re-adopt the fuel tank with its recorded litres, keep the radio key and every other ID, redo only the dailies that really failed, undo the manual drift and finish with a clean plan and no tainted objects.

mission.name: Pennywhistle Carousel Module Tree
mission.description: INCIDENT 0420 - Pennywhistle Clockwork Carousel Works. The workshop control plane was a single flat file; PR #88 restructured it into movements, stables (with a nested stalls module), compliance and finishes modules, retired null_resource in favour of terraform_data, renamed the "paint" module to "finishes" and dropped the scratch prototype run. The pipeline plan now wants to destroy and rebuild everything, including the ride licence, the stall load ratings on the brass plates and the oiling record, in the middle of a production week.
mission.objective: Make the refactored tree adopt the running works with zero destroys and zero re-issued values: describe every address change (flat to module, nested module, count index to named key, null_resource to terraform_data, renamed module and renamed resource inside it) with moved blocks, forget the prototype run without destroying it using a removed block, and end with a clean plan.
